definition_zh: 亲属关系；血亲与姻亲；亲切感、认同感；亲属制度研究
definition_en: the relationship between people who are related by blood or by marriage, or a feeling of closeness and shared identity
core_image: 一张织锦上两簇同色的线，一股从上一代直着下来，一股在两边横向打结。
scene: 织锦铺在桌上，中间一股线从上一代直着垂下，两侧另有几股横向打结，把两家人缝到一起。 The woven panel shows both kinship by blood and marriage ties between the two villages.
sceneCN: 这里 kinship 指「由血缘或婚姻连接起来的亲属关系」（第 1 个义项：血亲层面的亲属关系）；句意为这块织锦同时呈现两村之间的血亲与姻亲关系。可辨识物件：织锦、垂下的直线、横向的结、两侧的线团。

derivatives.zh: 古英语 cynn（家族、种类）→ 直接保留为「亲属；有亲属关系的」，语义收窄到人
kin + 属格 -s + man（人）→ 男性亲属，语义落在个体成员
kinsman 的 man 换为 woman → 女性亲属，语义仅改性别
kin + -red（古英语 rǣden「条件、状态」）→ 全体亲属，语义由个体转到集体
a-（表「属于」）+ kin → 同族的；引申为「相似的」，语义由血缘扩到性质

senses.title: Relation through blood
senses.definition: the tie between people descended from the same ancestor
senses.definitionCN: 出自同一祖先的人之间的纽带
senses.example: Kinship through the mother's line decides who inherits the orchard.
senses.exampleCN: 母系的血亲关系决定果园由谁继承。
senses.why: kin meant 'family, kind' in Old English, and -ship names a state, so kinship is literally the state of being of one family.
senses.whyCN: 古英语的 kin 意为「家族、种类」，-ship 表示状态，因此 kinship 字面就是「同属一家」的状态。

senses.title: Relation created by marriage
senses.titleCN: 由婚姻建立的姻亲关系
senses.definition: the tie created when a marriage joins two families, with its own duties and claims
senses.definitionCN: 婚姻把两家人联结起来所产生、自带义务与权利主张的纽带
senses.example: Their kinship began as an alliance of two farming households.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的姻亲关系起初是两个农耕家庭的结盟。
senses.why: the word covers anyone a family treats as related, so in-laws enter it as soon as the household counts them.
senses.whyCN: 这个词涵盖家庭当作亲属的所有人，因此一旦家庭把姻亲算进来，姻亲就进入此义。

senses.title: A feeling of closeness
senses.definition: a felt bond of warmth and understanding with someone who is not actually a relative
senses.definitionCN: 与并非真正亲属的人之间感到的温暖与理解纽带
senses.example: She felt a kinship with the strangers who had fled the same flood.
senses.exampleCN: 她与那些逃离同一场洪水的陌生人感到一种亲近。
senses.why: if shared descent makes people kin, shared experience can produce the same feeling, and the word follows the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 既然共同的血统使人成为亲属，共同的经历也能产生同样的感觉，词义便跟着感觉走。

senses.title: The study of kin systems
senses.definition: the branch of anthropology that compares how societies define relatives, descent and marriage
senses.definitionCN: 比较各社会如何界定亲属、世系与婚姻的人类学分支
senses.example: Kinship was the first subject taught in the new anthropology department.
senses.exampleCN: 亲属制度是新设人类学系最先开课的题目。
senses.why: once researchers compared many societies, the mass noun became a field of study rather than one family's tie.
senses.whyCN: 研究者比较众多社会之后，这个不可数名词就从一家人的关系变成一个研究领域。

senses.title: A relation between languages or ideas
senses.titleCN: 语言或思想上的同源关系
senses.definition: a shared origin or close structural relation between languages, ideas or works
senses.definitionCN: 语言、思想或作品之间共享的来源或紧密的结构关系
senses.example: The kinship of the two dialects shows in their verb endings.
senses.exampleCN: 两种方言的同源关系体现在动词词尾上。
senses.why: family trees serve both genealogists and linguists, so the word moves from people to anything that branches from one source.
senses.whyCN: 家谱树既供谱系学者用，也供语言学者用，于是这个词从人扩到任何由同一源头分出的东西。

senses.title: A close structural resemblance
senses.definition: a strong likeness between two things that suggests they belong to one family of forms
senses.definitionCN: 两物之间强烈相似，使人感到它们属于同一形式家族
senses.example: The kinship between the two poems lies in their shared metre.
senses.exampleCN: 两首诗近缘之处在于共用同一格律。
senses.why: descent can be replaced by resemblance: the word keeps the family shape but drops the ancestor.
senses.whyCN: 传承关系可被相似性替代：这个词保留家族的形状，却丢掉了祖先。

senses.title: A nation imagined as one family
senses.titleCN: 被想象成一个大家庭的民族
senses.definition: a shared national or ethnic identity expressed as brotherhood and common ancestry
senses.definitionCN: 以兄弟情谊与共同祖先表达的民族或族群认同
senses.example: The speech appealed to kinship among all the islanders.
senses.exampleCN: 演讲唤起全体岛民之间的同胞之情。
senses.why: politics borrows the warmth of the family word to make a large population feel related.
senses.whyCN: 政治借用了家庭词的温情，让大量人口感到彼此是亲属。

senses.title: A natural or spiritual affinity
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：人与物、人与地之间的天然契合
senses.definition: a deep affinity felt between a person and a place, an animal or a calling
senses.definitionCN: 人与地方、动物或使命之间感到的深切契合
senses.example: He speaks of his kinship with the river as if it were a relative.
senses.exampleCN: 他谈起自己与这条河的契合，仿佛那是位亲戚。
senses.why: the abstract end of the word keeps only affinity, with no genealogy behind it at all.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的抽象一端只保留契合，背后已完全没有谱系。

intro.en: Kinship joins kin, from Old English cynn 'family, kind', to the suffix -ship. Cynn goes back to Germanic *kunja-, and the deeper Indo-European form is a reconstruction.
intro.cn: kinship 由古英语 cynn「家族、种类」加后缀 -ship 构成。cynn 上承日耳曼语 *kunja-，更深的印欧语形式则属重构。

items.en: Cynn meant 'family, race, kind' and also 'nature, quality'; the recorded word already carried both the kin sense and the kind sense.
items.cn: cynn 意为「家族、族类、种类」，也指「本性、品质」；有记录的这个词已兼有亲属与种类两义。

items.en: The Germanic base *kunja- is generally regarded as the source of cynn and of cognates in the other Germanic languages.
items.cn: 一般认为日耳曼语词基 *kunja- 是 cynn 及其在其他日耳曼语中同源词的来源。

items.en: *Kunnan 'to know' is generally connected with *kunja-: a family is the group one knows and recognizes. English know is the same root.
items.cn: 一般认为 *kunnan「知道」与 *kunja- 相关：家族就是自己所认识、所认可的那群人。英语 know 同出这个词根。

items.en: *Ǵenh₁- 'to give birth, beget' is generally regarded as the deeper source of *kunja-, but the Indo-European form itself is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 一般认为 *ǵenh₁-「生育、产生」是 *kunja- 更深层的来源，但该印欧语形式本身属重构。

items.en: -ship, from Old English -scipe 'state, condition', turns a noun of persons into a noun of relation, as in kinship and friendship.
items.cn: -ship 出自古英语 -scipe「状态、情形」，把指人的名词变成指关系的名词，kinship 与 friendship 皆如此。

items.en: The compound is recorded from the Middle Ages; its use as the name of an anthropological field is a nineteenth-century specialization.
items.cn: 这个复合词在中世纪已有记录；把它用作人类学领域名称则是 19 世纪的专业化用法。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes, one of them a true relative with a different everyday sense; group two holds terms that name one part or one type of the same field.
note.cn: 第一组是形近词，其中一个是真同族词但日常义不同；第二组是只指同一领域某一部分或某种类型的词。

entries.definition: From the same cynn, but its everyday sense is 'type' or 'good-natured'; the family sense survives only in kindred and mankind.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 cynn，但日常义是「种类」或「和善的」；家族义只留在 kindred 与 mankind 里。

entries.definition: From Greek kinētikos 'of motion', built on kinein 'to move'; motion, not kinship, is its centre.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊语 kinētikos「运动的」，由 kinein「移动」构成；中心是运动，不是亲属关系。

entries.definition: A twist or bend, probably from Middle Dutch; the shared opening sound hides a totally different source.
entries.definitionCN: 扭结、弯折，可能来自中古荷兰语；相同的开头音掩盖了完全不同的来源。

entries.definition: From Turkish köşk 'pavilion', through French; it names a small booth and has no link to family.
entries.definitionCN: 经法语来自土耳其语 köşk「亭」，指小售货亭，与家族无关。

entries.definition: Relationship through marriage, or a natural attraction; it names one kind of tie, while kinship covers both kinds and the feeling as well.
entries.definitionCN: 通过婚姻形成的关系，或天然的吸引；它只指一种纽带，而 kinship 兼指两类关系与那种感觉。

entries.definition: Shared descent from a common ancestor, literally 'with the same blood'; marriage ties are excluded.
entries.definitionCN: 出自同一祖先的血统关系，字面为「同血」；姻亲关系不在其中。

entries.definition: The line traced from an ancestor to a descendant; kinship is the whole set of ties, descent only the vertical line.
entries.definitionCN: 从祖先追到后代的那条线；kinship 是全部纽带的集合，descent 只是纵向那条线。

entries.definition: The degree to which two people or populations share genes; it is a technical measure, not the social claim that kinship carries.
entries.definitionCN: 两人或两群体共享基因的程度；这是技术性度量，而非 kinship 自带的社会主张。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the recorded Old English noun, its Germanic relatives, and the English words built with the same two morphemes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：有记录的古英语名词、它的日耳曼同源词，以及用同两个语素造出的英语词。

normal.en: kin + -ship, exactly as friend + -ship: the suffix names a state of relation.
normal.cn: kin 加 -ship，正如 friend 加 -ship：后缀标出关系的状态。

normal.en: Old English cynn covered both 'family' and 'kind', which is why kind survives beside kin.
normal.cn: 古英语 cynn 兼指「家族」与「种类」，所以 kind 与 kin 至今并存。

normal.en: The same Germanic base gives English kin and German Kind 'child'.
normal.cn: 同一日耳曼语词基给出英语 kin 与德语 Kind「孩子」。

normal.en: *Kunnan 'know' explains the ancient link between knowing someone and counting them as family.
normal.cn: *kunnan「知道」解释了「认识某人」与「把某人算作家人」之间的古老联系。

normal.en: The fixed phrase 'a sense of kinship' shows the feeling sense plainly.
normal.cn: 固定搭配「一种亲近感」清楚显示了这个感觉义。

abstract.en: Picture a loom where one thread going down and one thread crossing are equally strong.
abstract.cn: 想象一台织机，一根向下的线与一根横穿的线一样结实。

abstract.en: Picture a stranger who reminds you of your sister, and the word that arrives before any reason.
abstract.cn: 想象一个让你想起姐姐的陌生人，以及那句先于任何理由出现的话。

abstract.en: Picture a language family drawn as a tree that grows downward from a single seed.
abstract.cn: 想象一个语系被画成一棵树，从一粒种子向下生长。

examples.en: Kinship ties still decide which family gets the water rights.
examples.cn: 亲属纽带仍然决定哪个家庭得到水权。

examples.en: The two composers share a kinship of style rather than of blood.
examples.cn: 这两位作曲家在风格上相近，而非血脉相连。

examples.en: Early anthropology mapped kinship before it mapped trade.
examples.cn: 早期人类学先绘制亲属关系，再绘制贸易路线。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「亲」与「ship」同船：亲属关系像一条船，把散在两岸的人装在一起 → 血亲、姻亲、亲近感

root: 古英语 cynn「家族、种类」< 日耳曼语 *kunja-，与 *kunnan「知道」（同源 know）相关；更深一般认为来自印欧语 *ǵenh₁-「生育」，该形式属重构。加 -ship 构成 kinship。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the fact of descent to the feeling of it: blood tie, marriage tie, felt closeness, the comparative study of such ties, shared origin in language, structural likeness, national brotherhood and finally affinity with a place.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「传承的事实」走向「传承的感觉」：血亲、姻亲、感到的亲近、对这类纽带的比较研究、语言上的同源、结构相似、民族同胞之情，最后是与地方的契合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a loom with one vertical thread of descent and one horizontal thread of marriage.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台织机，一根纵向的传承之线，一根横向的婚姻之线。

branches.en: TWO KINDS OF TIE: one inherited, one made by marriage, equally binding in daily life.
branches.cn: 两类纽带：一类继承而来，一类由婚姻造成，在日常生活中同样有约束力。

branches.en: WARMTH WRIT LARGE: the feeling of closeness, scaled from two people up to a whole nation.
branches.cn: 被放大的温情：亲近感从两个人扩展到整个民族。

branches.en: THE COMPARATIVE FIELD: many societies' rules studied side by side as one subject.
branches.cn: 比较领域：把众多社会的规则并置为一个学科来研究。

branches.en: SHARED ORIGIN IN THINGS: languages and works inherit, or merely resemble, one source.
branches.cn: 事物之间的同源：语言与作品或真继承同一源头，或只是彼此相像。

branches.en: PURE AFFINITY: no ancestor left, only the fit between a person and a place.
branches.cn: 纯契合：祖先已退场，只剩人与地方之间的相合。

intro.en: Kinship is the clearest case of an English word built from two native morphemes: a noun of family plus a suffix of state.
intro.cn: kinship 是英语本土语素构词最清楚的例子：一个表家族的名词加一个表状态的后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin relative here: kin is native Germanic, so the Latin list is empty by design, and the family is read through Old English and Germanic forms only.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁同族词：kin 是本土日耳曼词，因此拉丁词条按体例留空，整个词族只经古英语与日耳曼语形式来读。

items.structure: Old English cynn (noun), surviving unchanged in form
items.example: His kin live in the next valley.
Kinship carries duties as well as warmth.
items.exampleCN: 亲属关系既带来温情，也带来义务。

items.example: A kinsman spoke for the family at the hearing.
items.exampleCN: 一位男性亲属在听证会上代表家族发言。
她的女性亲属保存了那些信件。

items.example: The whole kindred came to the funeral.
items.exampleCN: 全体亲属都来参加了葬礼。

items.meaning: related by blood; similar in nature
items.meaningCN: 有血缘关系的；性质相似的
items.example: Their humour is akin to ours.
items.exampleCN: 他们的幽默感与我们的相近。

items.structure: Old English cynd (noun), same base as cynn
items.example: That kind of answer ends the argument.
Her kindliness made the room easy to enter.
items.exampleCN: 她的和善让那间屋子容易走进去。

definition_zh: 可疑的；有问题的；未必正确的；品行可疑的
definition_en: open to doubt, or not clearly acceptable
core_image: 一份文件上的签名，墨迹新得像是刚写上去的
scene: 董事会上，有人指出那笔交易的资金来源存在疑点。 At the board meeting someone pointed out that the source of the funds was questionable.
sceneCN: 这里 questionable 指可疑的（第 1 个义项：真实性存疑）；句意为董事会上，有人指出那笔交易的资金来源存在疑点。

pos.zh: 可疑的；有问题的；未必正确的；品行可疑的

senses.title: A questionable claim
senses.definition: a statement that may well be false
senses.definitionCN: 很可能不真实的陈述
senses.example: At the board meeting someone pointed out that the source of the funds was questionable.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会上，有人指出那笔交易的资金来源存在疑点。
senses.why: The first sense asks about truth, not morality.
senses.whyCN: 第一个义项问的是真假，不是道德。

senses.title: Questionable practices
senses.definition: conduct that may be legal but is hard to defend
senses.definitionCN: 可能合法却难以辩护的行为
senses.example: The auditor listed several questionable practices in the accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 审计师在账目里列出了几项有问题的做法。
senses.why: The word moves from fact to conduct without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从事实移到行为，形状不变。

senses.title: A questionable source
senses.definition: an origin that cannot be trusted to be accurate
senses.definitionCN: 不能保证准确的来源
senses.example: The story rested on a single questionable source.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇报道只靠一个来路可疑的消息源。
senses.why: The doubt here is about provenance, not about the reporter.
senses.whyCN: 这里的疑问针对来源，而不是记者本人。

senses.title: Questionable taste
senses.definition: a choice that others find vulgar or ill-judged
senses.definitionCN: 旁人觉得俗气或欠考虑的品味
senses.example: The decoration was not offensive, only questionable.
senses.exampleCN: 这装饰并不冒犯人，只是品味可疑。
senses.why: Here the judgement is aesthetic, not factual.
senses.whyCN: 这里评判的是审美，而不是事实。

senses.title: Open to question
senses.definition: not settled, and therefore fair to challenge
senses.definitionCN: 尚未确定，因此可以正当地质疑
senses.example: Whether the method scales up remains open to question.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方法能否放大，仍然存疑。
senses.why: The sense is procedural: the matter has not been closed.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是程序性的：事情还没有结案。

senses.title: A questionable victory
senses.definition: a success whose value or fairness is in doubt
senses.definitionCN: 价值或公平性存疑的成功
senses.example: It was a questionable victory, won on a technicality.
senses.exampleCN: 这是一场成色可疑的胜利，靠一个技术细节赢下。
senses.why: The result stands, but its worth does not.
senses.whyCN: 结果成立，它的价值却不成立。

senses.title: Questionable character
senses.definition: a person whose honesty has been doubted
senses.definitionCN: 诚实受到怀疑的人
senses.example: The witness was of questionable character and the jury knew it.
senses.exampleCN: 这名证人品行可疑，陪审团也知道。
senses.why: The oldest moral sense attaches to people, not facts.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的道德义项附着在人身上，而不是事实。

senses.title: Versus dubious
senses.definition: raising doubt, as opposed to feeling doubt
senses.definitionCN: 引起怀疑，与心怀怀疑相对
senses.example: A questionable deal makes you dubious about the seller.
senses.exampleCN: 一桩可疑的交易，会让你对卖家心生怀疑。
senses.why: The pair separates the object of doubt from the doubter.
senses.whyCN: 这一对词把怀疑的对象与怀疑者分开。

intro.en: Questionable is question plus -able, from Latin quaestio, 'a seeking or inquiry'.
intro.cn: questionable 是 question 加 -able，源头是拉丁语 quaestio（探询、审问）。

items.en: Quaerere meant to seek or ask.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻找或询问。

items.en: Quaestio named an inquiry or a legal examination.
items.cn: quaestio 指调查或法律审问。

items.en: French narrowed the word to a question asked.
items.cn: 法语把词义收窄为被提出的问题。

items.en: English added -able to mean fit to be questioned.
items.cn: 英语加上 -able，表示「可以被质疑的」。

items.en: The word now carries a hint of conduct as well as fact.
items.cn: 今天这个词既指事实，也带上一丝品行的意味。

note.en: The look-alike group is the quest- family; the near-meaning group separates dubious, suspect, debatable and doubtful.
note.cn: 形近组是 quest 词族；近义组把「可疑的」「有嫌疑的」「可争辩的」「不确定的」分开。

entries.definition: a request for information.
entries.definitionCN: 要求信息的提问。

entries.definition: a set of written questions.
entries.definitionCN: 一组书面问题。

entries.definition: a long search or pursuit.
entries.definitionCN: 漫长的寻找。

entries.definition: the act of taking by force.
entries.definitionCN: 以武力取得。

entries.definition: feeling or causing doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 感到或引起怀疑的。

entries.definition: believed to be guilty or false.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为有罪或虚假的。

entries.definition: open to argument.
entries.definitionCN: 可以争论的。

entries.definition: uncertain in outcome.
entries.definitionCN: 结果不确定的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a signature still wet on an old document.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「旧文件上一个还没干的签名」的画面。

normal.en: Questionable is question plus able: it invites a question.
normal.cn: questionable 是 question 加 able：它在邀请你提问。

normal.en: Picture a fresh signature on a document dated years ago.
normal.cn: 想象一份标着多年前日期的文件上有一个新鲜的签名。

normal.en: Say KWES-chun-a-bl; the middle syllable nearly vanishes.
normal.cn: 读 KWES-chun-a-bl，中间音节几乎消失。

normal.en: The word doubts without accusing: a gap, not a verdict.
normal.cn: 这个词只怀疑不指控：是一道缝，不是判决。

normal.en: Ask what exactly is in doubt: truth, conduct, taste or value?
normal.cn: 问清楚到底疑的是什么：真假、行为、品味还是价值？

abstract.en: Questionable is a polite word for a serious doubt.
abstract.cn: questionable 是对严重怀疑的礼貌说法。

abstract.en: It marks the space between what can be proved and what can be defended.
abstract.cn: 它标记「可证明」与「可辩护」之间的空隙。

abstract.en: The word protects the speaker: it raises a question without yet making a charge.
abstract.cn: 这个词保护说话者：提出问题，却尚未提出指控。

examples.en: The auditor listed several questionable practices in the accounts.
examples.cn: 审计师在账目里列出了几项有问题的做法。

examples.en: The story rested on a single questionable source.
examples.cn: 这篇报道只靠一个来路可疑的消息源。

examples.en: It was a questionable victory, won on a technicality.
examples.cn: 这是一场成色可疑的胜利，靠一个技术细节赢下。

dict_mnemonic.text: question（问题）+ able（能）→ 能被提出问题的，即可疑的。

root: 拉丁语 quaerere（询问）→ quaestio（审问）+ -able

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses ask what is in doubt: a claim, a practice, a source, a taste, an open matter, a victory, a character, and the difference from feeling dubious.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在问疑的是什么：说法、做法、来源、品味、未结之事、胜利、品行，以及与「心怀怀疑」的差别。

core.en: A SIGNATURE STILL WET
core.cn: 一个还没干的签名

branches.en: Truth of a statement and trust in its source.
branches.cn: 陈述的真假与对来源的信任。

branches.en: Conduct and character under quiet suspicion.
branches.cn: 被悄然怀疑的行为与品行。

branches.en: Aesthetic judgement that stays polite.
branches.cn: 保持礼貌的审美判断。

branches.en: Matters left open and successes of unclear value.
branches.cn: 未结之事与价值不明的成功。

branches.en: The object of doubt set against the doubter.
branches.cn: 怀疑的对象与怀疑者的对照。

intro.en: The quest- family runs from question and questionnaire to quest and conquest, all built on the Latin act of seeking.
intro.cn: quest 词族从 question、questionnaire 延伸到 quest、conquest，全都建立在拉丁语「寻找」的动作上。

latinIntro.en: Quaerere gives quaestio the noun and quaestus the search; English added -able to make the modern adjective.
latinIntro.cn: quaerere 给出名词 quaestio 与表示寻找的 quaestus；英语加上 -able 造出现代形容词。

definition_zh: n. 肉桂，桂皮；肉桂色（黄棕色）
definition_en: a sweet spice made from the bark of a tropical tree; a warm brown colour
core_image: 热饮里浮着一根卷曲的桂皮
scene: 热红酒里浮着一根肉桂。 A stick of cinnamon floated in the mulled wine.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：cinnamon 指肉桂；句意是热红酒里浮着一根肉桂。

senses.title: The spice
senses.definition: a sweet warm spice made from the dried bark of a tropical tree
senses.definitionCN: 用热带树皮干燥制成的香甜温热香料
senses.example: She added cinnamon to the apples.
senses.exampleCN: 她往苹果里加了肉桂。
senses.why: Greek kinnamomon named the bark long before English.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 kinnamomon 远早于英语就指这种树皮。

senses.title: The colour
senses.definition: a warm reddish-brown colour like the spice
senses.definitionCN: 像肉桂一样的暖红棕色
senses.example: The walls were painted cinnamon.
senses.exampleCN: 墙刷成了肉桂色。
senses.why: The spice gave its name to its own colour.
senses.whyCN: 这种香料把名字给了自己的颜色。

intro.en: Cinnamon comes through Greek kinnamomon and Latin from a Semitic name for the bark.
intro.cn: cinnamon 经希腊语 kinnamomon 与拉丁语，来自闪米特语对桂皮的称呼。

items.en: The name begins in a Semitic language.
items.cn: 这个名字起于一种闪米特语。

items.en: Greek borrows the name for the bark.
items.cn: 希腊语借入这个名称指桂皮。

items.en: Latin keeps the spice name.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留香料名。

items.en: English shortens it to cinnamon.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语缩为 cinnamon。

items.en: The spice trade spreads its use.
items.cn: 十七世纪香料贸易推广其用途。

items.en: Cinnamon also names a colour.
items.cn: 现代也指一种颜色。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cinn- opening; the near-meaning group lists warm spices.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cinn- 开头；近义组列出温热香料。

entries.definition: A red mineral.
entries.definitionCN: 朱砂。

entries.definition: A spice of the parsley family.
entries.definitionCN: 孜然。

entries.definition: Relating to cinnamon acid.
entries.definitionCN: 肉桂酸的。

entries.definition: A sweet spice from a seed.
entries.definitionCN: 肉豆蔻。

entries.definition: A strong dried flower bud.
entries.definitionCN: 丁香。

entries.definition: A fragrant spice in pods.
entries.definitionCN: 豆蔻。

normalIntro.en: A curled piece of bark that smells like warm kitchens.
normalIntro.cn: 一片卷起的树皮，闻起来像温暖的厨房。

normal.en: The name came through Greek.
normal.cn: 名字经希腊语传来。

normal.en: It is dried tree bark.
normal.cn: 它是干燥的树皮。

normal.en: A stick curls as it dries.
normal.cn: 干燥时卷成一根。

normal.en: It sweetens apples and wine.
normal.cn: 它给苹果和酒添甜香。

normal.en: The colour borrows the name.
normal.cn: 颜色也借用了这个名字。

abstract.en: Warmth you can smell.
abstract.cn: 能闻到的温暖。

abstract.en: A bark that learned to bake.
abstract.cn: 学会烘焙的树皮。

abstract.en: Brown with a memory of fire.
abstract.cn: 带着火之记忆的棕色。

examples.en: Dust the cake with cinnamon.
examples.cn: 在蛋糕上撒肉桂粉。

examples.en: Two cinnamon sticks simmered in the pot.
examples.cn: 锅里煮着两根桂皮。

examples.en: The scarf was a soft cinnamon brown.
examples.cn: 那条围巾是柔和的肉桂棕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「西拿门」——西边拿进门的一包桂皮。

root: 闪米特语 → 希腊语 kinnamomon → 拉丁语 → 英语 cinnamon

sensesIntro.en: The bark of a tropical tree became a spice, and the spice became a colour.
sensesIntro.cn: 热带树的树皮成了香料，香料又成了一种颜色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curled stick of bark steaming in a dark drink
core.cn: 核心意象：深色热饮里冒着热气的卷曲树皮

branches.en: A stick curling in hot wine.
branches.cn: 在热酒里卷曲的一根。

branches.en: Dust falling over baked apples.
branches.cn: 落在烤苹果上的粉末。

branches.en: A wall painted warm brown.
branches.cn: 刷成暖棕色的墙。

branches.en: A scarf the colour of toast.
branches.cn: 吐司色的围巾。

branches.en: A spice and its own shade.
branches.cn: 一种香料与它自己的色调。

intro.en: Cinnamon is a loan word; the list below adds words of spice, bark and scent.
intro.cn: cinnamon 是借词；下面列出香料、树皮与气味词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin cortex is bark and aroma is a sweet smell.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cortex 意为树皮，aroma 意为香气。

latinEntries.exampleCN: cortex 产生 cortex 与 cortical。
aroma 产生 aroma 与 aromatic。
species 产生 spice 与 special。

definition_zh: v. 体现；使具体化；是…的化身；包含；纳入
definition_en: to give a visible form to an idea, or to include something as part of a whole
core_image: 一座铜像立在广场中央，人物一手举着火炬一手按着一本打开的法典，抽象的条文变成了可以绕着走的形体
scene: 广场中央立着一座铜像，人物一手举火炬，一手按着一本打开的法典，孩子们绕着底座跑。 The statue embodies the idea of justice in bronze.
sceneCN: 这里 embody 指「体现」（第 1 个义项：把抽象理念变成可见形体）；句意是这座铜像把正义的理念铸进了青铜。

pos.zh: 体现；使具体化；是…的化身；包含

senses.title: To give a visible form
senses.definition: to express an idea or quality in a visible form
senses.definitionCN: （动词）把理念或品质表现为可见的形体
senses.example: The constitution embodies the principle that no one is above the law.
senses.exampleCN: 宪法体现了无人可凌驾于法律之上的原则。
senses.why: An abstract rule cast into a bronze figure that children can run around
senses.whyCN: 抽象规则被铸成一尊铜像，孩子们能绕着它跑

senses.title: To be a perfect example
senses.definition: to be a very good example of a quality
senses.definitionCN: （动词）成为某种品质的极好代表
senses.example: She embodies the patience that the job demands.
senses.exampleCN: 她体现了这份工作要求的那种耐心。
senses.why: One person in whom a whole quality stands up and walks
senses.whyCN: 一个人身上，一整种品质站起来走路

senses.title: To include as part of a whole
senses.definition: to include something as part of a larger whole
senses.definitionCN: （动词）把某物作为组成部分纳入更大的整体
senses.example: The treaty embodies the earlier agreement in its first chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 条约第一章纳入了先前的协议。
senses.why: A clause folded into a longer treaty like a page into a book
senses.whyCN: 一条条款被折进更长的条约，像一页纸折进书里

intro.en: Embody is em- plus body, from Old English bodig; to embody is to give an idea a body so that it can be seen and touched.
intro.cn: embody 由 em- 加 body 组成，body 来自古英语 bodig；embody 就是给理念一个身体，让它能被看见、被摸到。

items.en: Bodig means the trunk or the whole physical frame, and gives English body.
items.cn: bodig 意为躯干或整个身体，给出英语 body。

items.en: Body extends to a group of people and to the main part of a text.
items.cn: body 扩展到一群人，也扩展到文本的主体。

items.en: Embody appears in the 1540s, meaning to invest a spirit with a body.
items.cn: embody 出现于 16 世纪 40 年代，意为给灵魂赋予身体。

items.en: Embodiment is formed for the thing in which a quality is made visible.
items.cn: embodiment 构成，指某种品质得以显现的载体。

items.en: Embody is used for a person or work that perfectly represents an ideal.
items.cn: embody 用于指完美代表某种理想的人或作品。

items.en: Legal writing uses embody for including a rule inside a larger document.
items.cn: 法律文字用 embody 指把一条规则纳入更大的文件。

note.en: Embody, embodiment and bodily share the Germanic root bodig, a physical frame; incarnate and incorporate are the nearest synonyms.
note.cn: embody、embodiment 与 bodily 共享日耳曼词根 bodig（身体）；incarnate 与 incorporate 是最接近的同义词。

entries.definition: a thing that gives a quality visible form
entries.definitionCN: 体现；化身

entries.definition: relating to the physical body
entries.definitionCN: 身体的；肉体的

entries.definition: to make someone brave
entries.definitionCN: 使有胆量

entries.definition: given a human or physical form
entries.definitionCN: 化身的；具形的

entries.definition: to include something as part of a whole
entries.definitionCN: 纳入；合并

entries.definition: to be a perfect example of a quality
entries.definitionCN: 是…的化身；拟人化

normalIntro.en: Picture an abstract rule cast into a bronze figure that children can run around.
normalIntro.cn: 想象一条抽象的规则被铸成一尊铜像，孩子们能绕着它跑。

normal.en: A rule is cast into bronze and stands in a square.
normal.cn: 一条规则被铸成青铜，立在广场上。

normal.en: A torch in one hand and a law book in the other make the idea visible.
normal.cn: 一手火炬、一手打开的法典，让理念变得可见。

normal.en: Children run around the base and touch the cold metal.
normal.cn: 孩子们绕着底座跑，摸到冰凉的金属。

normal.en: Body is a frame, so the verb puts a frame around a thought.
normal.cn: 词根是身体，所以这个动词给想法套上一副身体。

normal.en: A clause is folded into a longer treaty like a page into a book.
normal.cn: 一条条款被折进更长的条约，像一页纸折进书里。

abstract.en: An abstract rule cast into a bronze figure that children can run around
abstract.cn: 抽象规则被铸成一尊铜像，孩子们能绕着它跑

abstract.en: One person in whom a whole quality stands up and walks
abstract.cn: 一个人身上，一整种品质站起来走路

abstract.en: A clause folded into a longer treaty like a page into a book
abstract.cn: 一条条款被折进更长的条约，像一页纸折进书里

examples.en: The constitution embodies the principle that no one is above the law.
examples.cn: 宪法体现了无人可凌驾于法律之上的原则。

examples.en: She embodies the patience that the job demands.
examples.cn: 她体现了这份工作要求的那种耐心。

examples.en: The treaty embodies the earlier agreement in its first chapter.
examples.cn: 条约第一章纳入了先前的协议。

dict_mnemonic.text: embody ＝ em-（使进入）＋ body（身体，古英语 bodig）＝「给理念一副身体」。三单 embodies，过去式与过去分词 embodied，现在分词 embodying；名词 embodiment 体现、化身；同族 body 身体、主体，bodily 身体的，bodiless 无实体的，disembody 使脱离肉体。三类用法：体现抽象 embody a principle 体现一条原则、embody the spirit of 体现…的精神、embody an ideal 体现一种理想；化身 she embodies patience 她是耐心的化身；纳入 embody in law 写进法律、the treaty embodies the clause 条约纳入该条款。近义 incarnate 强调赋予血肉形体，personify 强调某人恰是某品质的代表，incorporate 强调并入整体；embody 兼有使可见与纳入两义。注意与 embolden（使有胆量）拼写相近。

root: 古英语 bodig（躯干；身体）→ body ＋ em-（使进入）→ embody（体现；使具体化）

sensesIntro.en: Three ways a thought gets a body: bronze in a square, a quality walking in one person and a clause folded into a treaty.
sensesIntro.cn: 想法获得身体的三种方式：广场上的青铜、在一个人身上走动的品质，以及折进条约的条款。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an abstract rule cast into a bronze figure that children can run around
core.cn: 核心意象：抽象规则被铸成一尊铜像，孩子们能绕着它跑

branches.en: An idea is given a visible form.
branches.cn: 理念被赋予可见形体。

branches.en: A quality walks in one person.
branches.cn: 一种品质在一个人身上行走。

branches.en: A part is folded into a whole.
branches.cn: 一部分被折进整体。

branches.en: Both make the abstract stand up.
branches.cn: 两者都让抽象之物站起来。

branches.en: Both put a thing inside a body.
branches.cn: 两者都把东西放进一个形体。

intro.en: Embody is em- plus body; -ment gives embodiment, -ly gives bodily, dis- gives disembody and em- also gives embed.
intro.cn: embody 由 em- 加 body 组成；-ment 给出 embodiment，-ly 给出 bodily，dis- 给出 disembody，em- 也给出 embed。

latinIntro.en: The root body is Germanic, from Old English bodig; Latin corpus also means body and gives incorporate and corporeal.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 body 是日耳曼语，来自古英语 bodig；拉丁语 corpus 也意为身体，给出 incorporate 与 corporeal。

definition_zh: 使混乱；使昏乱；（蛋）变质；变糊涂
definition_en: to confuse someone's mind, or to go bad and rotten, as an egg does
core_image: 一枚放坏的蛋，摇起来浑浊一片
scene: 连考三门之后，他的脑子里只剩嗡嗡声，公式全搅成一团。 Too many formulas addled the student's brain.
sceneCN: 这里 addle 是「使混乱、使昏乱」（第 1 个义项：搅乱头脑）；句意为公式太多把学生的脑子搅浑了。

derivatives.zh: 由本词过去分词转形容词，义为「混乱的；糊涂的；（蛋）变质的」
由本词构成的复合形容词，义为「头脑混乱的」

senses.title: To confuse the mind
senses.definition: to make someone unable to think clearly
senses.definitionCN: 使某人无法清晰思考
senses.example: Too many formulas addled the student's brain.
senses.exampleCN: 公式太多把学生的脑子搅浑了。
senses.why: A rotten egg turns cloudy and useless; an addled mind is the same mixture where thought no longer separates.
senses.whyCN: 坏蛋变得浑浊无用；昏乱的头脑正是同样的混浊，思想再也无法分层。

senses.title: To go rotten, as an egg
senses.definition: of an egg, to spoil so that the contents turn mixed and cloudy
senses.definitionCN: 指鸡蛋变坏，内容物浑浊混合
senses.example: The eggs addled in the summer heat.
senses.exampleCN: 鸡蛋在暑热中放坏了。
senses.why: This is the original sense: the egg's clear parts collapse into one turbid mass.
senses.whyCN: 这是本源义：蛋里清澈的部分塌缩成一团浑浊。

intro.en: Addle comes from Old English adela, 'liquid filth, puddle', first used of eggs gone bad.
intro.cn: addle 源自古英语 adela（污水、浊液），最初用于变质的蛋。

items.en: adela meant 'filthy liquid or puddle'.
items.cn: adela 意为「污水、浊洼」。

items.en: Cousin forms in Germanic languages also name muddy liquid; the deeper root is uncertain.
items.cn: 日耳曼诸语言的同族词也指浑浊液体；更深的词根来源不确定。

items.en: addle described eggs whose contents had gone cloudy and spoiled.
items.cn: addle 描述内容物浑浊变坏的蛋。

items.en: The 'confused mind' sense grew from the rotten-egg picture.
items.cn: 「头脑混乱」义由坏蛋意象长出。

items.en: The adjective addled is now the commonest form, mostly of brains and thoughts.
items.cn: 形容词 addled 如今最常见，多用于头脑与思绪。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alike words of different roots; the second gathers words for confusion and spoilage.
note.cn: 第一组收词源不同但形近的词；第二组收表示混乱与变质的词。

entries.definition: A humorous old adjective for hopelessly confused.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「头昏脑胀的」，多见于旧式幽默文字。

entries.definition: An old nickname for a muddled person.
entries.definitionCN: 旧式称呼，义为「糊脑袋的人」。

entries.definition: A small venomous snake; only spelling near, root unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蝰蛇」；仅拼写相近，词源无关。

entries.definition: To mix things up into confusion.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「搅乱、弄混」。

entries.definition: To make someone dazed and unable to think.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使昏乱、使迷糊」。

entries.definition: To decay and go bad.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「腐烂、变坏」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the rotten-egg origin and the addled-brain collocation; the abstract hooks picture murky water.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用坏蛋的来源与 addled-brain 搭配；抽象记忆点想象浑浊的水。

normal.en: Addle began as bad egg liquid: adela, muddy water.
normal.cn: addle 起于坏蛋的浊液：adela，污水。

normal.en: Addle one's brain is the classic phrase.
normal.cn: addle one's brain 是经典搭配。

normal.en: The adjective addled describes both eggs and minds.
normal.cn: 形容词 addled 既形容蛋也形容头脑。

normal.en: Muddle rhymes with addle and means confusion too.
normal.cn: muddle 与 addle 押韵，同样表示混乱。

normal.en: It is informal and slightly humorous in modern use.
normal.cn: 现代用法偏非正式，略带幽默。

abstract.en: Picture an egg shaken into cloudy soup.
abstract.cn: 想象鸡蛋被摇成一碗浑汤。

abstract.en: Picture a pond stirred until nothing can be seen.
abstract.cn: 想象池塘被搅到什么都看不清。

abstract.en: Picture formulas swirling into grey fog in a head.
abstract.cn: 想象公式在头脑里旋成灰色迷雾。

examples.en: Too many formulas addled the student's brain.
examples.cn: 公式太多把学生的脑子搅浑了。

examples.en: The eggs addled in the summer heat.
examples.cn: 鸡蛋在暑热中放坏了。

examples.en: Late nights left him addled for the whole morning.
examples.cn: 熬夜让他整个上午昏昏沉沉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿豆」——豆浆搅浑了脑子也浑了，就是搅乱。

root: 古英语 adela（污水、浊液）；核心义是「清水变浑汤——蛋如此，头脑也如此」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from spoiling eggs to confusing minds, both by the same picture of turning clear into muddy.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从蛋的变质走到头脑的昏乱，共用同一幅「清变浑」的图景。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: clear water stirred into cloudy mud
core.cn: 核心意象：清水被搅成浑泥汤

branches.en: The mind stirred till thought will not settle.
branches.cn: 头脑被搅到思绪无法沉淀。

branches.en: The egg whose parts collapse into turbid mass.
branches.cn: 内容物塌成浑浊一团的蛋。

branches.en: Both senses are the same muddying, of egg or of mind.
branches.cn: 两个义项是同一场「变浑」，发生在蛋里或脑子里。

branches.en: This is the older, original sense.
branches.cn: 这是更古老的本源义。

branches.en: Modern usage keeps this sense alive mainly in addled.
branches.cn: 现代用法主要通过 addled 保留这个义项。

intro.en: Addle is a plain Germanic stem with no Latin prefix; the family is small and mostly English-made compounds.
intro.cn: addle 是单纯的日耳曼词干，没有拉丁前缀；词族很小，多为英语自造复合词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin kinship is recorded; the deeper Germanic root is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 无拉丁亲缘记录；更深的日耳曼词根来源不确定。

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「混乱的；（蛋）变质的」
复合形容词，义为「头脑混乱的」

definition_zh: 太阳能；由太阳辐射转化而来的能量
definition_en: energy that comes from the sun's radiation and is used for heat or electricity
core_image: 一片深色面板铺在屋顶上，正午的阳光穿过玻璃落到面板表面
scene: 正午的荒漠边缘，一排排深色面板把直射的日光收进电网。 The desert station runs entirely on solar energy.
sceneCN: 这里 solar energy 指「由太阳辐射得到的能量」（第 1 个义项：太阳发出的光和热被收集后用于供热或发电）；句意为这座沙漠观测站完全依靠太阳能运行。图中可辨识物件：倾斜的光伏面板、电缆、日光光斑、远处的沙丘。

pos.zh: 太阳能（不可数复合名词）

senses.title: Sunlight collected as usable power
senses.titleCN: 被收集起来的太阳辐射
senses.definition: the light and heat of the sun once it has been captured for heating or generating electricity
senses.definitionCN: 太阳发出的光和热被捕获后用于供热或发电的部分
senses.example: The desert station runs entirely on solar energy.
senses.exampleCN: 这座沙漠观测站完全依靠太阳能运行。
senses.why: solar names the sun as source and energy names the capacity to do work, so the phrase literally means work-capacity supplied by the sun.
senses.whyCN: solar 指明来源是太阳，energy 指明做功的能力，因此这个短语字面就是「由太阳供给的做功能力」。

senses.title: The resource itself
senses.definition: sunlight treated as a natural resource that countries and companies plan around
senses.definitionCN: 被当作自然资源来规划利用的太阳光
senses.example: The region treats solar energy as its cheapest resource.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区把太阳能当作最便宜的资源。
senses.why: once people plan how much of something to use, they speak of it as a resource, and sunlight enters that same accounting.
senses.whyCN: 当人们开始规划用多少，就会把它说成资源，太阳光也就进入了同一套账目。

senses.title: Electricity from photovoltaic cells
senses.definition: electric current produced when panels of semiconductor cells are struck by sunlight
senses.definitionCN: 半导体电池板受日光照射时产生的电流
senses.example: Rooftop panels converted solar energy into direct current.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶面板把太阳能转化成了直流电。
senses.why: the phrase narrows to electricity when engineers need a label for the input of a photovoltaic circuit.
senses.whyCN: 当工程师需要给光伏电路的输入端一个名称，这个短语就收窄为电力。

senses.title: Heat for water and buildings
senses.titleCN: 用于水和建筑的太阳热能
senses.definition: heat gathered from the sun to warm water, air or the interior of a building
senses.definitionCN: 从太阳收集来用于加热水、空气或建筑内部的热量
senses.example: The clinic heats its water with solar energy.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所利用太阳能加热水。
senses.why: heat is the older form of the phrase's use, since collectors warmed water long before panels made current.
senses.whyCN: 供热是这一短语更早的用法，因为在面板发电之前，集热器早已用来加热水。

senses.title: A policy and industry category
senses.definition: the sector, regulations and markets built around collecting the sun's power
senses.definitionCN: 围绕收集太阳能建立的行业、法规与市场
senses.example: The budget added tax credits for solar energy.
senses.exampleCN: 预算为太阳能增加了税收抵免。
senses.why: a physical input becomes a category when governments tax it, subsidize it and count jobs in it.
senses.whyCN: 当政府对其征税、补贴并统计就业，一种物理输入就变成了一个门类。

senses.title: Radiation in physics terms
senses.titleCN: 物理学意义上的太阳辐射
senses.definition: electromagnetic radiation emitted by the sun across a broad spectrum
senses.definitionCN: 太阳在宽广光谱范围内发出的电磁辐射
senses.example: Instruments measured solar energy across the visible spectrum.
senses.exampleCN: 仪器测量了可见光谱范围内的太阳辐射。
senses.why: physics keeps the literal reading and replaces 'usable' with a measurable flux of radiation.
senses.whyCN: 物理学保留字面读法，只把「可用」换成一个可测量的辐射通量。

senses.title: The emblem of clean power
senses.definition: a symbol used in debate for power that produces no smoke or carbon while running
senses.definitionCN: 在讨论中用来象征运行时不排烟、不排碳的电力
senses.example: The campaign put solar energy at the centre of its message.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动把太阳能放在其主张的中心。
senses.why: because the fuel arrives free and clean, the phrase came to stand for an entire environmental stance.
senses.whyCN: 因为燃料免费而清洁地到来，这个短语逐渐代表了一整套环保立场。

senses.title: Any free natural input
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何免费的自然输入
senses.definition: any freely arriving input that a system can convert into useful work
senses.definitionCN: 任何免费到来、可被系统转化为有用功的输入
senses.example: The team called public attention 'solar energy' for the project.
senses.exampleCN: 团队把公众的关注称作这个项目的「太阳能」。
senses.why: the metaphor works for anything that costs nothing to receive but needs a converter to become useful.
senses.whyCN: 凡是不花钱就能收到、却需要转换器才有用的东西，都适用这个比喻。

intro.en: Solar energy joins Latin sol 'sun' with Greek energeia 'activity'. Both elements came into English by separate learned routes, and the compound itself is a modern coinage. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: solar energy 把拉丁语 sol「太阳」与希腊语 energeia「活动」并置。两个成分分别经学术路径进入英语，整个复合词则是现代造词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sol was the Latin word for the sun and also the name of the sun god. Its deeper origin is not established; the Indo-European form often cited for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: sol 是拉丁语中表示太阳的词，也是太阳神的名字。其更深来源未得到证明；常被引用的印欧语形式属于重构形式。

items.en: Sol plus the adjective ending -alis produced solaris 'of the sun', which passed through Old French and Middle English as solar.
items.cn: sol 加形容词词尾 -alis 构成 solaris「太阳的」，经古法语与中古英语成为 solar。

items.en: Energeia meant 'activity, operation', built from en- 'in' and ergon 'work'. Aristotle used it for actuality as opposed to mere capacity.
items.cn: energeia 意为「活动、运作」，由 en-「在内」与 ergon「工作」构成。亚里士多德用它指现实，与单纯的能力相对。

items.en: Seventeenth-century writers borrowed energia for vigour of style, and physics later narrowed energy to the capacity for doing work.
items.cn: 17 世纪的作者借 energia 指文风的力度，物理学后来把 energy 收窄为做功的能力。

items.en: Solar energy became a fixed phrase in the nineteenth century, when solar engines and solar water heaters were described in the technical press.
items.cn: solar energy 在 19 世纪成为固定短语，当时技术刊物已在描述太阳能发动机与太阳能热水器。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin root of sol is unsettled, and the exact first appearance of the compound in print is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：sol 在拉丁语之前的词根无定论，这个复合词的确切最早书证也没有定说。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on Latin sol that look alike but do not all mean 'sun'; group two holds words for the same physical input under other names.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁 sol、形貌相近却并非都指「太阳」的词；第二组是同一物理输入的其他名称。

entries.definition: The adjective from sol, meaning 'of the sun'; it is the first element of the phrase, not a synonym for the whole phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 由 sol 来的形容词，意为「太阳的」；它是短语的第一个成分，不等同于整个短语。

entries.definition: Sol plus sistere 'to stand still': the moment the sun appears to stop in its yearly path.
entries.definitionCN: sol 加 sistere「停住」：太阳在周年路径上看似停住的那一刻，即至点。

entries.definition: A Latin word for a sun terrace, from sol; it is a place, not a form of power.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中指日光浴台的词，来自 sol；它指场所，不是能源。

entries.definition: From Latin solus 'alone', not sol 'sun'; the shared letters are coincidental and the words are unrelated in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 solus「独自」，而非 sol「太阳」；相同的字母只是巧合，两词词源无关。

entries.definition: The light itself as it arrives; solar energy names that light once it is captured for use.
entries.definitionCN: 指到达地面的光本身；solar energy 指这些光被捕获可供使用之后的形态。

entries.definition: Usually the electrical output of solar systems, where solar energy can also mean the heat input.
entries.definitionCN: 通常指太阳能系统的电力输出，而 solar energy 也可指热输入。

entries.definition: A wider class that includes solar, wind, water and biomass; solar energy is one member.
entries.definitionCN: 更宽的类别，包含太阳能、风能、水能与生物质能；太阳能是其中一员。

entries.definition: The adjective for the cell technology that turns light into current, not a name for the energy itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指把光变成电流的电池技术的形容词，并非能量本身的名称。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: sol 'sun' + -ar 'of': the phrase begins with the Latin name of the sun itself.
normal.cn: sol「太阳」+ -ar「…的」：短语开头就是太阳的拉丁名。

normal.en: Greek ergon 'work' is hidden inside energy, so energy means work-capacity.
normal.cn: energy 里藏着希腊 ergon「工作」，所以 energy 就是做功的能力。

normal.en: The family runs solar, solar energy, solar power, solar panel, solar cell.
normal.cn: 同族说法包括 solar、solar energy、solar power、solar panel、solar cell。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the industry: solar energy system, solar energy storage, solar energy industry.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出产业义：太阳能系统、太阳能储存、太阳能产业。

normal.en: The same sol root appears in solstice and solarium, both about the sun's position.
normal.cn: 同一 sol 词根出现在 solstice 与 solarium 中，都与太阳的位置有关。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf that never sends a bill for the light it uses.
abstract.cn: 想象一片叶子，从不为自己用的光开账单。

abstract.en: Picture a roof that quietly turns noon into a battery's stored afternoon.
abstract.cn: 想象一片屋顶，把正午悄悄变成电池里储存的下午。

abstract.en: Picture a currency that is minted every morning whether or not anyone works.
abstract.cn: 想象一种货币，不管有没有人干活，每个早晨都会新铸出来。

examples.en: The village pumps its water with solar energy.
examples.cn: 这个村庄用太阳能抽水。

examples.en: Solar energy avoids the fuel costs of a diesel generator.
examples.cn: 太阳能免去了柴油发电机的燃料成本。

examples.en: The course explains how solar energy becomes household current.
examples.cn: 这门课讲解太阳能如何变成家庭用电。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「solar（太阳的）+ energy（能量）」——太阳送来的能量 → 太阳能

root: 拉丁 sol「太阳」+ 形容词词尾 -aris/-al；energy 来自希腊 energeia「活动、运作」= en-「在内」+ ergon「工作」。sol 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one flow: radiation arrives, is captured, becomes heat or current, then is counted as a resource, an industry, a scientific quantity, a political emblem and finally a metaphor for any free input.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条流程展开：辐射到达、被捕获、变成热或电流，随后被计为资源、产业、科学量、政治象征，最后成为任何免费输入的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark panel on a roof receiving noon light and passing it into wires.
core.cn: 核心意象：屋顶上的深色面板接住正午的光，把它送进电线。

branches.en: PHYSICAL ARRIVAL: radiation reaches a surface, whether measured in a lab or gathered on a roof.
branches.cn: 物理到达：辐射抵达表面，无论是在实验室测量还是在屋顶收集。

branches.en: RESOURCE: the arriving light is entered into plans and budgets as a supply.
branches.cn: 资源：到达的光被记入规划与预算，成为一种供给。

branches.en: CONVERTED FORMS: the same input leaves as electric current or as stored heat.
branches.cn: 转换形态：同一输入以电流或储存的热离开。

branches.en: INDUSTRY: laws, subsidies and markets turn the physical flow into a sector.
branches.cn: 产业：法律、补贴与市场把物理流动变成一个行业。

branches.en: EMBLEM AND METAPHOR: the phrase stands for clean politics, then for any free natural gift.
branches.cn: 象征与比喻：短语代表清洁政治，再引申为任何免费的自然馈赠。

intro.en: Solar energy is a compound of two learned borrowings: a Latin adjective and a Greek-derived noun. Its parts still build other English words, so the phrase can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: solar energy 是两个学术借词的复合：一个拉丁形容词加一个希腊来源名词。其成分仍在构成其他英语词，因此这个短语可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Sol gives solar, solstice and solarium; Greek ergon, through energeia, gives energy, energetic and energize.
latinIntro.cn: sol 衍生 solar、solstice 与 solarium；希腊 ergon 经 energeia 衍生 energy、energetic 与 energize。

items.structure: Latin noun sol, solis (m., third declension)
items.example: The root names the source of the whole phrase.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名了整个短语的来源。

items.example: Solar means belonging to the sun.
A solar collector faces the noon sun.
items.exampleCN: 太阳能集热器朝向正午的太阳。

items.example: The Greek noun supplied the scientific term for work-capacity.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词提供了表示做功能力的科学术语。

items.example: The panel converts light into electrical energy.

items.meaningCN: 太阳供给的能量；太阳能
items.example: The desert station runs entirely on solar energy.
items.exampleCN: 这座沙漠观测站完全依靠太阳能运行。

items.meaningCN: 由光产生电流的；光伏的

latinEntries.structure: energia, -ae (f., first declension; from Greek energeia)

definition_zh: 灵长类学家；研究灵长类行为、生态与演化的学者
definition_en: a scholar who studies primates, their behaviour, ecology and evolution
core_image: 一个人在同一棵树下坐了二十年，能叫出三代的猴子，也能背出它们的关系
scene: 同一只母猴被跟了二十年，记录者给它取了名字，也给它建了档案。 The primatologist knew three generations of one family by their faces.
sceneCN: 这里指「研究灵长类的学者」（第 2 个义项：长期野外研究者）；句意为这位灵长类学家凭脸就认得一个家族的三代成员。

pos.zh: 灵长类学家（可数，复数 primatologists）

collocations.zh: 灵长类学家的田野笔记
灵长类学家与保护工作者

derivatives.zh: primatologist 的学科基座：primate + -logy → 灵长类学
拉丁 primas「居首者」→ 灵长类
etho-（希腊 ethos「习性」）+ -logist（研究者）→ 动物行为学家（语义偏移：以行为为界，不以类群为界）
zoo-（希腊 zōion「动物」）+ -logist → 动物学家（语义偏移：范围更宽）

senses.title: A practitioner of the field
senses.titleCN: 学科从业者：以灵长类学为业的人
senses.definition: a person who works professionally in primatology
senses.definitionCN: 以灵长类学为职业的人
senses.example: The primatologist knew three generations of one family by their faces.
senses.exampleCN: 这位灵长类学家凭脸就认得一个家族的三代成员。
senses.why: -ist marks the agent, so the word names whoever does what primatology describes, exactly as biologist names the doer of biology.
senses.whyCN: -ist 标记施动者，因此这个词指做灵长类学所述之事的人，正如 biologist 指做 biology 的人。

senses.title: A long-term field researcher
senses.titleCN: 长期野外研究者：在同一站点跟踪同一群体
senses.definition: one who follows the same group at one site for years or decades
senses.definitionCN: 在同一站点多年乃至数十年跟踪同一群体的人
senses.example: As a field primatologist she could tell half the troop by voice alone.
senses.exampleCN: 作为野外灵长类学家，她只听声音就能认出群中一半个体。
senses.why: The discipline's signature method is individual recognition over time, and the person who holds that method is named by the same title.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科的标志方法是跨越时间的个体识别，而掌握该方法的人就以同一头衔称呼。

senses.title: A laboratory experimentalist
senses.titleCN: 实验室研究者：做认知与比较实验
senses.definition: one who runs controlled experiments on captive primates
senses.definitionCN: 对圈养灵长类做受控实验的人
senses.example: The primatologist in the psychology building never set foot in a forest.
senses.exampleCN: 心理学楼里的这位灵长类学家从未进过森林。
senses.why: The same animal can be studied as a mind, and laboratories produced a second kind of practitioner with different training and different arguments.
senses.whyCN: 同一种动物可作为心智来研究，实验室因此造出第二类从业者，其训练与争论方式都不同。

senses.title: A conservation advocate
senses.titleCN: 保护倡导者：把研究用于种群存续
senses.definition: one who applies the field's data to protecting threatened populations
senses.definitionCN: 把研究数据用于保护受威胁种群的人
senses.example: The primatologist testified that the road would split one population in two.
senses.exampleCN: 这位灵长类学家作证说，那条路会把一个种群切成两半。
senses.why: Because the subjects are often endangered, the researcher's knowledge becomes evidence in land-use decisions; advocacy is a role the title now covers.
senses.whyCN: 由于研究对象常属濒危，研究者的知识成了土地利用决策中的证据；倡导是该头衔如今覆盖的一个角色。

senses.title: A teacher and supervisor
senses.titleCN: 教师与导师：培养学生、主持研讨
senses.definition: one employed to teach the subject and supervise research students
senses.definitionCN: 受雇教授该学科并指导研究学生的人
senses.example: The primatologist taught one course and supervised four dissertations.
senses.exampleCN: 这位灵长类学家教一门课，指导四篇学位论文。
senses.why: Once the field entered universities, the practitioner acquired the duties of a salaried academic, which the fieldworker's title did not previously imply.
senses.whyCN: 学科进入大学之后，从业者获得领薪学术人员的职责，而田野工作者的头衔此前并不含这些。

senses.title: An author of monographs
senses.titleCN: 专著作者：把长期观察写成书
senses.definition: the writer of a book-length account of one group or site
senses.definitionCN: 把对一个群体或站点的长期观察写成整本书的人
senses.example: The primatologist took eleven years to publish the monograph on the troop.
senses.exampleCN: 这位灵长类学家花了十一年才出版关于这个猴群的专著。
senses.why: Long-term data only become knowledge when written up, and the discipline's classic products are single-site books, so authorship is built into the role.
senses.whyCN: 长期数据只有写成文字才成为知识，而本学科的经典成品是单站点著作，因此著述已写进这个角色里。

senses.title: A consultant for zoos and agencies
senses.titleCN: 顾问：为动物园与管理部门提供判断
senses.definition: one who advises zoos, parks or agencies on primate care and policy
senses.definitionCN: 就灵长类饲养与管理政策向动物园、公园或部门提供意见的人
senses.example: The zoo hired a primatologist to redesign the enclosure around social groups.
senses.exampleCN: 动物园请了一位灵长类学家，按社会群体重新设计展区。
senses.why: Captive primates live in institutions, and institutions need expert judgment about grouping and enrichment; the title travels into practical settings.
senses.whyCN: 圈养灵长类生活在机构里，机构在分组与丰容上需要专家判断；这个头衔于是走进实务场景。

senses.title: A public communicator
senses.titleCN: 公共传播者：向大众讲述研究
senses.definition: one who explains primate research to the public through film, radio or writing
senses.definitionCN: 通过影片、广播或写作向大众解释灵长类研究的人
senses.example: The primatologist's radio series made a remote forest familiar to millions.
senses.exampleCN: 这位灵长类学家的广播系列让一片遥远森林为千百万人所熟悉。
senses.why: A field about charismatic animals produces public figures as well as papers, and the same title covers the person in front of a camera.
senses.whyCN: 研究有魅力动物的领域既产出论文，也产出公众人物，同一个头衔也覆盖镜头前的那个人。

intro.en: Primatologist is the field name plus the Greek agent ending, filtered through Latin and French; the only unsettled part is when the field name itself was coined.
intro.cn: primatologist 是学科名加希腊施动词尾，经拉丁语与法语过滤而成；唯一未定的部分是学科名本身何时造出。

items.en: Primas 'of the first rank' comes from primus 'first' and named leading men and later leading bishops; the zoological use of the stem dates from Linnaeus's order name.
items.cn: primas「居首的」出自 primus「第一」，先指显要人物，后指首席主教；该词干在动物学中的使用始于林奈的目名。

items.en: -Logia 'account, study' derives from logos 'word, reason' and legein 'to gather, say'; the deeper root is reconstructed.
items.cn: -logia「叙述、学问」出自 logos「言词、理性」与 legein「收集、说出」；更深词根为重构。

items.en: The agent ending reached English through Latin -ista and French -iste, from Greek -istes, and marks the person devoted to the stem's activity.
items.cn: 该施动词尾经拉丁 -ista、法语 -iste，源自希腊 -istes 进入英语，标记专注于词干所述活动的人。

items.en: Primatology is recorded from the mid-twentieth century, and primatologist followed once the field had journals and posts.
items.cn: primatology 的书证起于 20 世纪中期；待该领域有了期刊与职位，primatologist 随即出现。

items.en: Long-term field stations and university chairs turned a research topic into a career with its own training path.
items.cn: 长期野外站与大学教席把一个研究题目变成有自身训练路径的职业。

items.en: Source uncertain: no single first citation is agreed for either word, and Linnaeus's motive for Primates is inferred, not documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定：两个词都没有公认的最早书证；林奈以 Primates 命名的动机属推断，并无文献说明。

note.en: Group one holds the same-stem words most often swapped for the person; group two holds neighbouring specialists.
note.cn: 第一组是最常与人称互换的同词干词；第二组是相邻的专门研究者。

entries.definition: The discipline itself; the person is named by adding the agent ending.
entries.definitionCN: 学科本身；指人须加施动词尾。

entries.definition: A member of the order under study; it is the object, never the researcher.
entries.definitionCN: 被研究的那个目的成员；是对象，绝不是研究者。

entries.definition: The capitalized plural names the order, not a group of people.
entries.definitionCN: 首字母大写的复数命名目，不是一群人。

entries.definition: Describes work belonging to the field; it cannot stand for the worker.
entries.definitionCN: 描述属于该领域的工作，不能指工作者。

entries.definition: A specialist in animal behaviour as such, not in one taxonomic group.
entries.definitionCN: 专门研究动物行为本身，而非某一分类类群。

entries.definition: A specialist in animals generally; primatologists are zoologists with a narrow object.
entries.definitionCN: 泛研究动物的专家；灵长类学家是对象较窄的动物学家。

entries.definition: A specialist in human societies and biology; the neighbour who shares questions about tool use.
entries.definitionCN: 研究人类社会与生物学的专家；在工具使用问题上共享疑问的邻居。

entries.definition: One who works to protect species and habitats, often without research training in the group.
entries.definitionCN: 致力于保护物种与栖息地的人，常无该类群的研究训练。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real roles and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实角色与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: -ist marks the person, exactly as in biologist and zoologist.
normal.cn: -ist 标记人，与 biologist、zoologist 完全同理。

normal.en: The person is named after the method: someone who can recognise every individual in a troop.
normal.cn: 此人以方法得名：能认出群中每一只个体的人。

normal.en: The family runs primatology, primatologist, primatological, primate, Primates, ethologist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 primatology、primatologist、primatological、primate、Primates、ethologist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: a field primatologist, a primatologist's field notes, a team of primatologists.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：野外灵长类学家、灵长类学家的田野笔记、灵长类学家团队。

normal.en: The title travels: forest, laboratory, zoo, courtroom, radio studio.
normal.cn: 这个头衔会走动：森林、实验室、动物园、法庭、广播间。

abstract.en: Picture a person who knows a family's faces better than her own relatives' faces.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人对猴子家族的脸比对自家亲戚的脸更熟。

abstract.en: Picture a notebook in which the same individual appears at three different ages.
abstract.cn: 想象一本笔记，同一只个体以三个年龄出现。

abstract.en: Picture a scientist translating a forest into a sentence a city can hear.
abstract.cn: 想象一位科学家把森林翻译成城市听得懂的一句话。

examples.en: The primatologist argued that the group had been observed long enough to count as a genealogy.
examples.cn: 这位灵长类学家主张，这个群体已被观察得足够久，可以当作一份家谱。

examples.en: A primatologist was called in when the sanctuary could not stop the fights.
examples.cn: 收容所止不住打斗时，请来了一位灵长类学家。

examples.en: Primatologists disagree about how much of primate behaviour can be generalised to people.
examples.cn: 灵长类学家对灵长类行为有多少可推及人类存在分歧。

dict_mnemonic.text: prim（第一）+ at（形容词）+ logist（研究者）＝ 研究灵长目的学者；记「同一棵树下坐二十年」。

root: 拉丁 primas「居首者」（来自 primus「第一」）+ 希腊 -logia「学问」+ 希腊 -istēs（经拉丁 -ista、法语 -iste）施动词尾；确切首见年代来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one person through the places the title reaches: the practitioner, the field researcher, the laboratory experimenter, the advocate, the teacher, the author, the consultant and the public voice.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一个人走过这个头衔能到的地方：从业者、野外研究者、实验室研究者、倡导者、教师、著者、顾问与公共声音。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person who has sat under the same tree for twenty years and can name three generations of monkeys.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人在同一棵树下坐了二十年，能叫出三代猴子的名字。

branches.en: PERSON AND METHOD: the title names whoever does the field's work, and the work is long-term recognition.
branches.cn: 人与方法：头衔指做这门学问之事的人，而那件事是长期识别。

branches.en: THE SECOND ROOM: controlled experiments create a different kind of practitioner.
branches.cn: 第二个房间：受控实验造出另一类从业者。

branches.en: OUTSIDE THE CAMPUS: testimony about a road, and advice on an enclosure.
branches.cn: 校园之外：就一条路作证，就一处展区给建议。

branches.en: TEACHING AND WRITING: students supervised, and the single-site book that takes a decade.
branches.cn: 教学与写作：被指导的学生，与耗时十年的单站点著作。

branches.en: THE VOICE: the same title covers the person in front of a camera.
branches.cn: 声音：同一个头衔也覆盖镜头前的人。

intro.en: The noun is the field name plus a Greek agent ending, and nearly every near neighbour differs only by its suffix.
intro.cn: 这个名词是学科名加希腊施动词尾，几乎每个近邻词都只差一个后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin primas supplies the stem; Greek -logia and -istes supply the rest, with Latin -ista and French -iste as intermediaries. Latin contributes no additional root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 primas 提供词干；希腊 -logia 与 -istes 提供其余部分，拉丁 -ista 与法语 -iste 为中介。拉丁语不提供额外词根。

items.example: The stem builds primate and primacy alike.
items.exampleCN: 该词干同样构成 primate 与 primacy。

items.example: Primate is the object of the practitioner's work.
items.exampleCN: primate 是从业者的研究对象。

items.example: The ending separates the person from the field.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾把人从学科中分出。

items.example: The discipline supplies the title's base.
The word names a career and a role.
items.exampleCN: 这个词命名一种职业与角色。

items.example: The adjective marks the work, not the worker.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词标记工作，而非工作者。

items.example: The neighbour is defined by behaviour rather than group.
items.exampleCN: 邻居以行为而非类群界定。

items.example: The suffix marks an aim, not a discipline.
items.exampleCN: 该后缀标记目的，而非学科。
