definition_zh: 质子；原子核中带一个单位正电荷的稳定粒子；氢原子核
definition_en: a stable particle found in every atomic nucleus, carrying one unit of positive electric charge
core_image: 一颗带正电的小球被一层中和的云裹着，云散开后它独自露出来，仍牢牢占着中心的位置
scene: 云室里，宇宙射线留下一条粗短的白色轨迹。 A proton knocked loose by a cosmic ray left a thick track in the cloud chamber.
sceneCN: 这里 proton 指「原子核中带正电的粒子」（第 1 个义项：原子核内带一个单位正电荷的稳定粒子）；句意：一个被宇宙射线撞出的质子在云室里留下一条粗而短的轨迹。图中可辨识物件：云室、铅板、白色轨迹、实验台。

derivatives.zh: 使质子化；向分子加入质子

senses.title: The positive particle of the nucleus
senses.titleCN: 原子核中带正电的粒子
senses.definition: the stable particle that carries one unit of positive charge inside an atomic nucleus
senses.definitionCN: 原子核内部带一个单位正电荷的稳定粒子
senses.example: Every nucleus except ordinary hydrogen holds at least one proton.
senses.exampleCN: 除普通氢以外，每一种原子核都至少含有一个质子。
senses.why: The Greek name means 'first', and the proton was the first nuclear particle to be identified, so it took that name.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词本义为「第一」，而质子是最早被辨认出的核内粒子，因此得了这个名字。

senses.title: A hydrogen nucleus on its own
senses.definition: a hydrogen nucleus stripped of its electron, which is exactly one proton
senses.definitionCN: 失去电子后的氢原子核，也就是单独的一个质子
senses.example: Strip the electron from a hydrogen atom and only a proton remains.
senses.exampleCN: 把电子从氢原子上剥离，剩下的就只有质子。
senses.why: Hydrogen is the one element whose nucleus is a single proton, so the general name also names that simplest case.
senses.whyCN: 氢是唯一核内只有一个质子的元素，因此这个通名也直接指最简单的那个情形。

senses.title: The count that fixes an element
senses.titleCN: 决定元素身份的那个数量
senses.definition: the number of protons in a nucleus, which determines which chemical element it is
senses.definitionCN: 原子核中的质子数目，决定它属于哪种化学元素
senses.example: Add one proton and the element changes into the next one in the table.
senses.exampleCN: 增加一个质子，元素就变成周期表里的下一种。
senses.why: A chemical reaction may move electrons but never changes this count, so the count became the identity card of an element.
senses.whyCN: 化学反应可以搬动电子，却改不了这个数目，于是这个数目成了元素的身份证明。

senses.title: A hydrogen ion in acid chemistry
senses.titleCN: 酸化学里被交出的氢离子
senses.definition: a bare hydrogen ion that an acid gives away to another substance
senses.definitionCN: 酸交给另一种物质的裸氢离子
senses.example: In the modern definition, an acid is any substance that can give up a proton.
senses.exampleCN: 按现代定义，凡能交出一个质子的物质都是酸。
senses.why: A hydrogen ion without its electron is a proton, so chemistry borrowed the nuclear name for the thing an acid hands over.
senses.whyCN: 失去电子的氢离子就是一个质子，因此化学界借用了核物理的称呼，来指酸交出的那个东西。

senses.title: A beam aimed at a tumour
senses.titleCN: 用于治疗肿瘤的质子束
senses.definition: a stream of accelerated protons used as a medical tool that can be stopped at a chosen depth
senses.definitionCN: 把质子加速成束，作为能在选定深度停下的医疗工具
senses.example: The clinic chose proton treatment because the beam stops inside the tumour.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所选用质子治疗，因为粒子束会在肿瘤内部停下。
senses.why: Protons lose energy in a predictable way, so a beam can be aimed to spare the healthy tissue behind it.
senses.whyCN: 质子的能量损失有可预测的规律，因此束流可以被瞄准，从而避开其后方的健康组织。

senses.title: A fast visitor from space
senses.titleCN: 从太空高速到访的质子
senses.definition: a high-energy proton arriving from outer space as part of cosmic radiation
senses.definitionCN: 作为宇宙辐射的一部分，从外层空间高速抵达的高能质子
senses.example: A single cosmic proton can trigger a shower of secondary particles.
senses.exampleCN: 一个宇宙质子就能引发一连串次级粒子。
senses.why: Cosmic rays are mostly protons, so astronomy uses the ordinary nuclear word for these travellers.
senses.whyCN: 宇宙射线主要由质子组成，天文学便用这个平常的核物理词来称呼这些远行者。

senses.title: The charged stream of the solar wind
senses.titleCN: 太阳风里的带电粒子流
senses.definition: one of the charged particles that the sun continuously sends out into space
senses.definitionCN: 太阳持续抛向太空的带电粒子之一
senses.example: The solar wind is a thin gas of protons and electrons.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳风是质子与电子组成的稀薄气体。
senses.why: The solar wind is ionized hydrogen, so its positive half is simply protons.
senses.whyCN: 太阳风是电离的氢，其中带正电的那一半就是质子。

senses.title: The fuel of the proton chain in stars
senses.definition: a proton taking part in the fusion chain that powers stars like the sun
senses.definitionCN: 参与聚变链式反应、为太阳这类恒星供能的质子
senses.example: Four protons must combine before one helium nucleus appears in the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 在太阳内部，要四个质子合起来才会出现一个氦核。
senses.why: The chain of reactions begins with protons, so the whole stellar process is named after them.
senses.whyCN: 这条反应链从质子开始，因此整个恒星过程以它命名。

intro.en: Proton is Greek, built from prōtos 'first' with the particle ending -on that physics later fixed in place. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词是希腊语词，由「第一」加粒子命名惯用的词尾构成；年代均为约数。

items.en: Prōtos meant 'first, foremost', built on pro 'before, in front'. Its deeper origin is not reconstructed with confidence.
items.cn: prōtos 意为「第一、最前的」，由表示「在前」的成分构成。它更早的来源无法稳妥地重构。

items.en: The neuter form prōton meant 'the first thing'. Ancient writers used it for a first principle, long before physics existed.
items.cn: 中性形式 prōton 意为「第一者」。古代作者用它指第一原理，远在物理学出现之前。

items.en: When the lightest nucleus was identified around 1919 to 1920, the old word for a first thing was revived for it.
items.cn: 大约在 1919 至 1920 年间最轻的核被确认时，这个表示「第一者」的旧词被重新启用。

items.en: As the neutron was named by contrast, the positive partner kept the name proton, and the pair became the two nucleons.
items.cn: 中子作为对照被命名后，带正电的搭档保留质子之名，两者合称核子。

items.en: The first recorded uses for the modern particle sense are approximate; the word itself is ancient, the meaning is about a century old.
items.cn: 现代粒子义的最早书证年代为约数；词本身古老，而这一含义只有约一百年。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close to proton but come from other roots; group two holds the particles it is measured against.
note.cn: 第一组是形音相近却另有词源的词；第二组是常与它相比较的其他粒子。

entries.definition: From Greek phōs, phōtos 'light' plus the same particle ending: a quantum of light, with no charge at all.
entries.definitionCN: 由希腊语「光」加同一个粒子结尾构成：光的一个量子，完全不带电荷。

entries.definition: Coined from Greek prōteios 'primary', which rests on the same prōtos 'first': a primary substance of living tissue, not a particle.
entries.definitionCN: 由希腊语「首要的」造出，而这个词又出自同一个「第一」：指生命组织的首要成分，与粒子无关。

entries.definition: Greek prōtos 'first' plus agōnistēs 'competitor': the leading figure in a drama, from the same first-word root.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语「第一」加「竞争者」：戏剧中的首要人物，与质子的「第一」同源。

entries.definition: Greek prōtos 'first' plus typos 'impression': the first model of a thing, not a nuclear particle.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语「第一」加「印痕」：某物的首个模型，与核粒子无关。

entries.definition: The nucleon with almost the same mass and no electric charge; proton and neutron together make up nearly all nuclear mass.
entries.definitionCN: 质量几乎相同但不带电的核子；质子与中子共同构成几乎全部核质量。

entries.definition: The light negative particle that orbits the nucleus; its charge balances the proton's charge in a neutral atom.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕原子核运动的轻质负电粒子；在中性原子里，它的电荷与质子相抵。

entries.definition: The covering word for either kind of nuclear particle, so a proton is one sort of nucleon.
entries.definitionCN: 对两种核内粒子的统称，因此质子是核子的一种。

entries.definition: A whole atom or molecule that has gained or lost electrons; a lone proton is the smallest positive ion.
entries.definitionCN: 获得或失去电子的整个原子或分子；单独的质子是最小的正离子。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek prōtos 'first' plus the particle ending -on: the first particle of the nucleus.
normal.cn: 希腊语「第一」加粒子结尾：核内第一个被认出的粒子。

normal.en: The proton sets the element's number, so its count is the identity of the atom.
normal.cn: 质子数决定元素，因此这个数目就是原子的身份。

normal.en: The family runs proton, protonic, protonate, protonation, antiproton.
normal.cn: 同族词包括质子、质子的、使质子化、质子化、反质子。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark its uses: proton beam, proton therapy, proton donor.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用途：质子束、质子治疗、质子供体。

normal.en: The same first-root appears in protein, protagonist and prototype, all from Greek prōtos.
normal.cn: 同一个「第一」词根出现在蛋白质、主角与原型中，都出自希腊语。

abstract.en: Picture a numbered seat that decides which row the whole theatre belongs to.
abstract.cn: 想象一个带编号的座位，它决定整个剧场属于哪一排。

abstract.en: Picture one lamp at the centre of a dark hall, giving light but never taking it.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗大厅中央的一盏灯，只给光，不取光。

abstract.en: Picture the first brick laid, whose position names the wall that follows.
abstract.cn: 想象砌下的第一块砖，它的位置为后面整堵墙命名。

examples.en: The nucleus of carbon holds six protons and six neutrons.
examples.cn: 碳的原子核含六个质子与六个中子。

examples.en: Chemists describe an acid as a proton donor.
examples.cn: 化学家把酸描述为质子供体。

examples.en: The sun burns by turning protons into helium.
examples.cn: 太阳靠把质子变成氦来发光。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pro（在前）+ ton（吨）」——最前面那块最重的砖，就是质子

root: 希腊 prōtos「第一」+ 粒子命名惯用的词尾；prōtos 更早的来源不明。英语形式即本词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start with the charged core of the atom, move to the bare hydrogen nucleus and the element count, then follow the same particle into acids, hospitals, cosmic rays, the solar wind and finally the sun's fusion chain.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从原子带正电的核心出发，转到单独的氢核与元素编号，再让同一个粒子依次进入酸、医院、宇宙射线、太阳风，最后进入太阳的聚变链。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one positively charged brick at the centre of every atom, and the same brick alone in the simplest atom.
core.cn: 核心意象：每个原子中心一块带正电的砖，而在最简单的原子里只有这一块砖。

branches.en: ONE BRICK: whether inside a heavy nucleus or alone as hydrogen, the same charged brick is being named.
branches.cn: 同一块砖：无论在重核内部还是单独作为氢，被命名的都是这块带正电的砖。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: the count of bricks is written down as the name of the element.
branches.cn: 账本：砖的数目被记成元素的名称。

branches.en: THE HANDOVER: chemistry treats the brick as a token that an acid gives away.
branches.cn: 交出：化学把这颗砖当作酸可以递出去的凭物。

branches.en: THE TRAVELLER: the same brick is aimed at a tumour, arrives from space, or streams out of the sun.
branches.cn: 远行者：同一颗砖或被瞄准肿瘤，或从太空抵达，或从太阳流出。

branches.en: THE FURNACE: in stars the brick becomes fuel, and four of them must meet to make helium.
branches.cn: 熔炉：在恒星里这砖成了燃料，四颗相会才能造出氦。

intro.en: Proton is a Greek noun, but its first-root and its particle ending both recur across scientific and everyday English.
intro.cn: 质子是希腊语名词，但它的「第一」词根与粒子结尾在科学与日常英语里都反复出现。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin cognate of proton; the Latin word for first, primus, belongs to another family. The Greek forms below are the true parts.
latinIntro.cn: 质子没有拉丁同族词；拉丁语里表示「第一」的 primus 属于另一个词族。真正的构件是下面的希腊语形式。

items.example: The prefix marks whatever comes first in a series.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出系列中最先出现的那一个。

items.example: The adjective ranks one item ahead of all others.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词把某一项排在所有其他项之前。

items.example: The proton sits at the centre of the atom.
The protonic charge balances the electron cloud.
items.exampleCN: 质子的电荷与电子云相抵。

items.meaning: to add a proton to a molecule
items.example: The acid protonates the base within microseconds.
items.exampleCN: 酸在微秒之内就使碱质子化。

items.meaning: a primary substance of living tissue
items.meaningCN: 生命组织里的首要成分
items.example: Protein was named as the first substance of the body.
items.exampleCN: 蛋白质曾被命名为身体的首要物质。

items.example: The protagonist speaks first in every act.
items.exampleCN: 主角在每一幕里都最先开口。

items.meaning: the first model of a device
items.example: The prototype was tested before any copies were made.
items.exampleCN: 原型在任何复制品造出之前先接受了测试。

definition_zh: 食物网；多条食物链交织成的取食关系网络
definition_en: the network formed when many feeding links among species are shown together, rather than one linear sequence
core_image: 同一片水塘的取食关系被画成一张网：藻类连向小虾与螺，鱼连向两者，鹭连向鱼与螺
scene: 同一片水塘里，鱼除了吃虾也吃水生昆虫，鹭既吃鱼也吃螺，关系被画成一张交叉的网。 A food web shows all of these feeding links at once instead of one line.
sceneCN: 这里指多条取食关系交织成的网络（第 1 个义项：整体取食网络）；句意为食物网把这些取食关系一次性全部展示出来，而不是只画一条线。

pos.zh: 某一群落完整的取食关系网络

derivatives.zh: 该短语的前半，源自古英语表示食物的词，义为「食物」
该短语的后半，源自古英语表示织物的词，义为「网」
由该短语换成表示「链」的后半构成的相邻术语，义为「食物链」，指单条路径
由该短语与「模型」组合而成，义为「食物网模型」，指用于计算与预测的网络模型
食物网研究中的指标，由表示「连接」的词加性质名词词尾构成，义为「连接度」
食物网研究中的性质，由表示「杂食」的词加性质名词词尾构成，义为「杂食性」，指同时取食多个营养级

senses.title: A network of feeding links
senses.definition: the whole set of feeding links among the species of a community, shown as a network rather than a line
senses.definitionCN: 一个群落内全部取食关系的集合，以网络而非单线的形式呈现
senses.example: A food web for the estuary contains more than ninety species.
senses.exampleCN: 这片河口的食物网包含九十多个物种。
senses.why: Many chains share species, so a line cannot hold them and a net had to be named.
senses.whyCN: 多条链共享物种，一条线装不下，于是必须给一张网命名。

senses.title: Species as nodes and feeding as links
senses.titleCN: 物种为节点、取食为连线
senses.definition: a structure of nodes, usually species or populations, joined by directed links that record who eats whom
senses.definitionCN: 由节点（通常是物种或种群）与记录「谁吃谁」的有向连线构成的结构
senses.example: Each arrow in the food web points from the eaten to the eater.
senses.exampleCN: 食物网里的每个箭头都从被吃的一方指向取食的一方。
senses.why: A network needs points and connections before it can be counted, so species and meals became those two things.
senses.whyCN: 网络要有节点与连接才能计数，于是物种与取食成了那两样东西。

senses.title: A closer picture than the chain
senses.titleCN: 比食物链更接近真实的图景
senses.definition: a representation that keeps the alternative pathways and the omnivory a single chain must leave out
senses.definitionCN: 保留替代路径与杂食性的表示法，而单条链必须把这些略去
senses.example: The food web revealed that the fish also feeds on seeds.
senses.exampleCN: 这张食物网揭示出鱼也取食种子。
senses.why: Omnivory is common in the field, and a model that forbids it cannot describe a real community.
senses.whyCN: 杂食在野外很常见，禁止杂食的模型无法描述真实群落。

senses.title: Measured by connectance and link density
senses.titleCN: 以连接度与连接密度度量
senses.definition: a network summarised by how many links exist relative to the possible number, and by links per species
senses.definitionCN: 以实际连线相对于可能连线的比例、以及每个物种的连线数来概括的网络
senses.example: Two lakes with the same species differ in food web connectance.
senses.exampleCN: 两个物种相同的湖泊，在食物网连接度上并不相同。
senses.why: Two webs can look alike and behave differently, so ratios of links were invented to tell them apart.
senses.whyCN: 两张网可能看着相似却行为不同，于是发明了连线比例来区分。

senses.title: A framework for keystone effects
senses.definition: a structure in which the removal of one well-connected node propagates through many others
senses.definitionCN: 在其中移除一个连接众多的节点会波及许多其他节点的结构
senses.example: Removing the kelp took the food web apart from the bottom.
senses.exampleCN: 移除海藻，等于从底部把这食物网拆开。
senses.why: Effects travel along the arrows, and the network shows which arrows exist.
senses.whyCN: 影响沿箭头传播，而网络显示了哪些箭头存在。

senses.title: A tool for modelling and management
senses.definition: a quantitative object built into simulations used to predict the effects of fishing, planting or removal
senses.definitionCN: 被写入模拟以预测捕捞、种植或移除后果的定量对象
senses.example: Managers ran the food web model to test three fishing rules.
senses.exampleCN: 管理者运行食物网模型，检验三条捕捞规则。
senses.why: A picture is not a prediction, so the web was turned into numbers for simulation.
senses.whyCN: 图景不是预测，于是把网转成数字用于模拟。

senses.title: An indicator of stability
senses.definition: a network whose redundancy and weak links are read as measures of how far disturbance will spread
senses.definitionCN: 其冗余与弱连接被用来判断扰动会传播多远的网络
senses.example: A food web with many weak links absorbed the drought better.
senses.exampleCN: 一张弱连接众多的食物网更好地吸收了这次干旱。
senses.why: Redundancy decides how far a shock travels, and the web makes redundancy visible.
senses.whyCN: 冗余决定冲击传播多远，而网让冗余变得可见。

senses.title: Different webs in different habitats
senses.definition: a network differing between soil, fresh water and open sea, and including the microbial loop
senses.definitionCN: 在土壤、淡水与开阔海域各自不同，并包含微生物环的网络
senses.example: The soil food web is built on fungi and bacteria rather than on leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤食物网建立在真菌与细菌之上，而不是叶片之上。
senses.why: Soil and water are run by different organisms, so the same term had to be applied to unlike networks.
senses.whyCN: 土壤与水由不同生物运转，同一个术语因此被用到截然不同的网络上。

senses.title: Built from gut contents and isotopes
senses.titleCN: 由胃含物与同位素数据构建
senses.definition: a network estimated from what animals contain, what stable isotopes show and what field observation records
senses.definitionCN: 由动物体内残留、稳定同位素结果与野外观察记录估计出来的网络
senses.example: They rebuilt the food web after analysing the stomachs of forty fish.
senses.exampleCN: 他们分析了四十条鱼的胃之后重建了这张食物网。
senses.why: A web is an estimate assembled from evidence rather than an observed object, so its construction became part of its definition.
senses.whyCN: 网是由证据拼出的估计，而不是被观察的物体，因此构建方式成了定义的一部分。

intro.en: Food is a native Germanic noun and web is the old word for woven cloth. The compound applies the image of weaving to feeding, and became standard ecology in the twentieth century.
intro.cn: 前半「食物」是日耳曼本族名词，后半「网」是表示织物的古老词。这个复合词把「编织」的形象用到取食上，二十世纪成为生态学标准术语。

items.en: Foda meant food, related to the verb for feeding.
items.cn: 这个词意为食物，与表示「喂养」的动词同源。

items.en: Webb meant woven cloth, and it also named the spider's net.
items.cn: 这个词意为织物，也用来指蜘蛛的网。

items.en: Wefan meant to weave, and the noun kept the sense of threads crossing each other.
items.cn: 这个词意为编织，名词保留了「线彼此交叉」的意思。

items.en: A web of threads crossing in many directions is the opposite of a chain's single line, and the image needed no explanation.
items.cn: 一张向多方交叉的线网正好与链的单线相反，这个比喻无需解释。

items.en: Ecologists adopted the compound for the full set of feeding links in a community, and the phrase became standard after the nineteen twenties.
items.cn: 生态学家采用这个复合词表示一个群落全部取食关系，这个短语在二十世纪二十年代之后成为标准说法。

note.en: The first group shares food or web; the second group names the analytical quantities used to describe a network.
note.cn: 第一组共用 food 或 web；第二组是描述网络时所用的分析量。

entries.definition: Nourishment, the first element.
entries.definitionCN: 养料，是前半部分。

entries.definition: A woven network, the second element.
entries.definitionCN: 编织成的网，是后半部分。

entries.definition: A linked set of pages; the same web image in a different industry.
entries.definitionCN: 指相互链接的页面集合；同一个「网」的意象用于另一个行业。

entries.definition: A spider's net, the literal source of the image.
entries.definitionCN: 指蜘蛛网，是这一意象的字面来源。

entries.definition: To marry; historically related to pledging rather than weaving, a common false friend.
entries.definitionCN: 指结婚；历史上与「立誓」而非「编织」有关，是常见的误认同源。

entries.definition: One linear path through the network.
entries.definitionCN: 指网络中的一条线性路径。

entries.definition: A feeding position, a way of summarising nodes in a web.
entries.definitionCN: 指取食位置，是概括网中节点的一种方式。

entries.definition: The general mathematical object of nodes and links.
entries.definitionCN: 指由节点与连线构成的一般数学对象。

entries.definition: A simulation of a whole system, of which the food web is one part.
entries.definitionCN: 指整个系统的模拟，食物网是其中一部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use weaving, the contrast with the chain, and the measurements ecologists take.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「编织」、与链的对照，以及生态学家所取的度量。

normal.en: Web says threads crossing in many directions, which is why it replaced the single line.
normal.cn: 「网」说的是向多方交叉的线，这正是它取代单线的原因。

normal.en: Nodes are species, arrows are meals: the whole picture is a map of eating.
normal.cn: 节点是物种，箭头是取食关系，整幅图就是一张取食地图。

normal.en: Connectance is links present divided by links possible.
normal.cn: 连接度等于已存在的连线除以可能存在的连线。

normal.en: Remove a well-connected node and the effect travels along many arrows at once.
normal.cn: 移除一个连接众多的节点，影响会沿许多箭头同时传播。

normal.en: The soil food web runs on fungi and bacteria, not on leaves.
normal.cn: 土壤食物网靠真菌与细菌运转，而不是靠叶片。

abstract.en: A web is a structure of dependencies, and its weakness is also its strength: many paths mean many routes for failure and for recovery.
abstract.cn: 网是一种依赖结构，它的弱点也是它的强处：多条路径既意味着多条失败的路线，也意味着多条恢复的路线。

abstract.en: The chain answers what eats what next; the web answers what happens if one thing stops.
abstract.cn: 链回答接下来谁吃谁，网回答如果某一样停下来会怎样。

abstract.en: Every arrow is a transfer of stored sunlight, and the web is the accounting of that light.
abstract.cn: 每个箭头都是一次储存阳光的转移，而网就是对这份阳光的核算。

examples.en: The food web of the marsh includes three species of snail.
examples.cn: 这片沼泽的食物网包含三种螺。

examples.en: Pesticides simplified the food web long before the birds declined.
examples.cn: 农药在鸟类数量下降之前很久就已简化了这张食物网。

examples.en: Researchers mapped the food web from stomach contents and isotope ratios.
examples.cn: 研究者根据胃含物与同位素比值绘制了食物网。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「富德 韦布」——富德是食物，韦布是织成的网，把吃与被吃织成一张网，就是食物网

root: 古英语 fōda「食物」；古英语 webb「织物、网」← wefan「编织」。两词在二十世纪生态学中组合为固定术语，表示一个群落全部取食关系，与单线的「食物链」相对。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses describe one network from several angles: its links, its nodes, its realism, its measurements, its keystone effects, its use in models, its stability, its habitats and how it is built.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从多个角度描述同一张网：连线、节点、真实性、度量、关键种效应、模型用途、稳定性、生境差异与构建方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pond's feeding relations drawn as crossing threads, algae to snail and shrimp, fish to both, heron to fish and snail.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片水塘的取食关系画成交叉的线，藻类连向螺与虾，鱼连向两者，鹭连向鱼与螺。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the whole set of links, with species as nodes and meals as arrows.
branches.cn: 对象：全部连线的集合，物种为节点，取食为箭头。

branches.en: THE REALISM: alternative pathways and omnivory that a single chain cannot hold.
branches.cn: 真实：单条链容纳不下的替代路径与杂食性。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: connectance and links per species, which let two webs be compared.
branches.cn: 度量：连接度与每物种连线数，使两张网可以比较。

branches.en: THE USE: keystone effects travelling through the network, and models used to test rules.
branches.cn: 用途：在网中传播的关键种效应，以及用来检验规则的模型。

branches.en: THE READING: stability from weak links, habitat-specific webs, and construction from guts and isotopes.
branches.cn: 读法：由弱连接看稳定性、各生境不同的网，以及由胃含物与同位素构建。

intro.en: Both elements are native English, so the compound is Germanic in build even though its science is modern.
intro.cn: 两个成分都是英语本族词，因此尽管这门科学是现代的，这个复合词的构造属日耳曼式。

latinIntro.en: Neither element has a Latin source, so the Latin entries are left empty rather than filled with approximations.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都没有拉丁语来源，因此拉丁语词条留空，而不是用近似形式填充。

items.example: It is the recorded source of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 它是该名词有记录的来源。

items.example: It is the structure the web replaces.
items.exampleCN: 它是被网取代的那种结构。

items.example: It names a species in the model.
items.exampleCN: 它命名模型中的一个物种。

items.meaning: the share of possible links that exist
items.meaningCN: 已存在连线占可能连线的比例
items.example: It is the standard network measure.

items.meaning: the stone that holds an arch
items.example: It names a species whose removal collapses the structure.
items.exampleCN: 它命名移除后会使结构崩塌的物种。

derivatives.zh: 由该短语换成表示「链」的后半构成，义为「食物链」
由该短语与「模型」组合而成，义为「食物网模型」
由表示「连接」的词加性质名词词尾构成，义为「连接度」
由表示「杂食」的词加性质名词词尾构成，义为「杂食性」

definition_zh: 振幅；广阔；充足
definition_en: the largeness or fullness of something; the height of a wave from its middle line
core_image: 声波从静线荡开的最大摆幅
scene: 技术员调高旋钮，波形在屏上拔高。 The engineer turned the dial to increase the amplitude of the signal wave.
sceneCN: 这里的 amplitude 是「振幅」（第 1 个义项：波峰到中线的距离）；句意是工程师转动旋钮增大了信号波的振幅。

derivatives.zh: 同根形容词，义为「充足的；宽敞的」
由同根 ampl- 派生，义为「放大；增强」
由 amplify 派生，义为「放大；扩充」

senses.title: The height of a wave or vibration
senses.definition: in physics, the maximum distance a wave or vibration moves from its central position
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中波或振动偏离中心位置的最大距离
senses.example: Louder sounds have waves of greater amplitude.
senses.exampleCN: 更响的声音其波的振幅更大。
senses.why: The Latin root ampl- means large; the largeness of a swing from the rest line is exactly amplitude.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 ampl- 意为「大」；摆动偏离静线的幅度之大，正是振幅之义。

senses.title: Largeness or breadth in general
senses.definition: the quality of being large, broad, or extensive, especially of space or range
senses.definitionCN: 空间或范围上的大而广，如视野、疆域的辽阔
senses.example: The amplitude of the savanna stretched to the horizon.
senses.exampleCN: 稀树草原的辽阔一直延伸到地平线。
senses.why: Once the word means measurable largeness, any broad extent can be described by it.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词表示「可度量的大」，任何广阔的范围便都能用它来描述。

senses.title: Fullness of supply or mind
senses.definition: abundance or richness, as of knowledge, style, or provision
senses.definitionCN: 知识、文风或供应上的丰富充盈
senses.example: He spoke with amplitude, drawing on years of reading.
senses.exampleCN: 他旁征博引，讲得充实丰沛。
senses.why: Largeness applied to knowledge or style becomes richness and fullness of expression.
senses.whyCN: 「大」用在学识或文风上，就成了表达的丰富与充盈。

intro.en: Amplitude comes from Latin amplitudo, largeness, formed on amplus, large.
intro.cn: amplitude 来自拉丁语 amplitudo「广大」，由 amplus「大」加抽象名词后缀 -tudo 构成。

items.en: The older root behind amplus is uncertain; links to filling or spreading have been proposed.
items.cn: amplus 更早的词根存疑，一说与「充满、铺展」相关。

items.en: Latin amplus meant large, and amplitudo meant largeness or magnificence.
items.cn: 拉丁语 amplus 意为「大」，amplitudo 意为「广大、宏伟」。

items.en: French amplitude carried the word into learned usage.
items.cn: 法语 amplitude 使该词进入学术用法。

items.en: English adopted amplitude in the 16th century for greatness of extent.
items.cn: 英语 16 世纪借入 amplitude，表示范围之广大。

items.en: Physics later fixed the word for the peak distance of a wave, now its dominant sense.

entries.definition: to make larger or louder

entries.definition: height above sea level

entries.definition: a way of feeling or thinking

entries.definition: great size or importance
entries.definitionCN: 大小；量级，同为 -itude 度量名词

entries.definition: the extent of variation

entries.definition: a very large quantity

entries.definition: smallness of amount or quality

abstract.cn: 想象一道波从平直中线高高扬起。

abstract.en: Picture a plain so wide that roads seem like threads.
abstract.cn: 想象一片旷野，公路细如丝线。

abstract.en: Feel a lecture brimming with citations and stories.
abstract.cn: 感受一场旁征博引、充实丰沛的讲座。

definition_zh: 陆地的；陆生的；地球的；陆栖的；类地的
definition_en: relating to the land or the earth, living on land rather than in water or in trees, or belonging to the planet Earth
core_image: 森林地面的苔藓间爬着甲虫，头顶是树冠，几步之外的溪水里另有生物
scene: 林下的苔藓和甲虫都生活在陆地上，与溪水里的生物全然不同。 Mosses and beetles on the forest floor are terrestrial life, unlike the creatures in the stream.
sceneCN: 这里 terrestrial 指「生活在陆地上的」（第 1 个义项：陆生动物，与水生相对）；句意：林下的苔藓与甲虫是陆生生命，和溪水中的生物不同。图中可辨识物件：苔藓层、甲虫、落叶、几步外的溪流。

pos.zh: 陆地的；陆生的；地球的；陆栖的；类地的
陆地生物；地球人（少见，多用于科幻或生态分类）

derivatives.zh: 陆生动物饲养箱；玻璃花房

senses.title: Animals that live on land
senses.definition: describing animals that live mainly on dry land rather than in water
senses.definitionCN: 描述主要在干燥陆地上而非水中生活的动物
senses.example: Mosses and beetles on the forest floor are terrestrial life, unlike the creatures in the stream.
senses.exampleCN: 林下的苔藓与甲虫是陆生生命，和溪水中的生物不同。
senses.why: the Latin root terra means dry land, and ecology uses the adjective to mark the medium an animal occupies, contrasting it with aquatic.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 terra 意为干燥陆地，生态学用这个形容词标记动物所占的介质，与 aquatic 相对。

senses.title: Plants that grow on land
senses.definition: describing plants rooted in soil in the air rather than submerged or floating in water
senses.definitionCN: 描述扎根土壤、暴露在空气中，而非沉水或浮水的植物
senses.example: Terrestrial plants had to evolve a waxy cuticle to hold moisture.
senses.exampleCN: 陆生植物必须演化出蜡质角质层来保住水分。
senses.why: botany applies the same land-and-air label to plants, where the decisive contrast is with aquatic and epiphytic growth.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把同一个「陆地加空气」的标签用于植物，关键对照是水生与附生。

senses.title: Of the planet Earth
senses.definition: relating to the earth as a planet, especially in contrast with other worlds
senses.definitionCN: 与作为行星的地球有关，尤与其它世界相对
senses.example: Terrestrial life may be the only life in this solar system.
senses.exampleCN: 地球生命也许是这个太阳系里唯一的生命。
senses.why: the adjective moves from land to the whole globe when the comparison shifts from water to space.
senses.whyCN: 当比较对象从水变成太空时，这个形容词便从陆地扩展到整个地球。

senses.title: Land as opposed to sea
senses.definition: belonging to dry land as a physical realm, as in terrestrial transport or terrestrial borders
senses.definitionCN: 属于干燥陆地这一物理领域，如陆路运输、陆地边界
senses.example: The isthmus is the narrowest terrestrial link between the two seas.
senses.exampleCN: 这条地峡是两海之间最窄的陆上通道。
senses.why: this sense treats land as a surface for movement and boundaries, so terrestrial pairs with maritime and aerial.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项把陆地看作通行与划界的表面，因此 terrestrial 与 maritime、aerial 构成系列。

senses.title: Rocky planets like Earth
senses.titleCN: 类地行星（以岩石为主的行星）
senses.definition: describing planets made mainly of rock and metal, with solid surfaces, rather than gas giants
senses.definitionCN: 描述主要由岩石与金属构成、有固体表面的行星，区别于气态巨行星
senses.example: Mars and Venus are the other terrestrial planets of the inner system.
senses.exampleCN: 火星与金星是内太阳系另外两颗类地行星。
senses.why: astronomy reuses the land word for bodies with a solid surface, since a rocky planet is land writ large.
senses.whyCN: 天文学把「陆地」一词用于有固体表面的天体，因为岩石行星就是放大的陆地。

senses.title: Ground-based broadcasting or networks
senses.titleCN: 地面（而非卫星）的广播与通信
senses.definition: describing communication systems based on land stations rather than satellites or cables
senses.definitionCN: 描述以陆地站点而非卫星或海底光缆为基础的通信系统
senses.example: Terrestrial broadcasting still reaches farms beyond the fibre network.
senses.exampleCN: 地面广播仍能覆盖光纤网络之外的农场。
senses.why: the sense extends land-based physical infrastructure to radio and television, where the ground station anchors the network.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项把陆基实体设施扩展到广播电视，地面站是网络的锚点。

senses.title: Ground-dwelling rather than tree-dwelling
senses.definition: in ecology, describing species that forage or live on the ground rather than in the canopy
senses.definitionCN: 生态学中指在地面觅食或栖息、而非在树冠层的物种
senses.example: The reserve protects both terrestrial and arboreal primates.
senses.exampleCN: 保护区同时保护地栖与树栖的灵长类。
senses.why: within land habitats the adjective is narrowed further: ground is the medium, and arboreal is its opposite.
senses.whyCN: 在陆地生境内部，这个形容词进一步收窄：地面是介质，树栖是它的对立面。

senses.title: Of land ecosystems as a category
senses.titleCN: 陆地生态系统的（与水域生态相对）
senses.definition: used for ecosystems, carbon pools and biodiversity found on land, as opposed to aquatic or marine ones
senses.definitionCN: 指陆地上的生态系统、碳库与生物多样性，与水生态或海洋生态相对
senses.example: Terrestrial carbon storage depends heavily on soil depth.
senses.exampleCN: 陆地碳储量在很大程度上取决于土壤深度。
senses.why: global-change science needs a cover term for all land systems, so terrestrial becomes the standard label for that pool.
senses.whyCN: 全球变化研究需要统称所有陆地系统，terrestrial 因而成为这一集合的标准标签。

intro.en: Terrestrial comes from Latin terrestris 'of the earth', built on terra 'dry land, earth' plus the suffix -estris. English adopted it in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: terrestrial 来自拉丁 terrestris「大地的」，由 terra「干燥陆地、大地」加后缀 -estris 构成，16 世纪进入英语。

items.en: Terra meant 'dry land, earth, soil'. Its own origin is debated; a connection with a root meaning 'to dry' is often proposed but remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: terra 意为「干燥陆地、大地、土壤」。其自身来源有争议；常有人提出它与表示「干燥」的词根有关，但这仍是假说。

items.en: The adjective terrestris 'of the earth, earthly' was formed with -estris, and it contrasted with marine and celestial things.
items.cn: 形容词 terrestris「大地的、尘世的」由 -estris 构成，与海洋的、天界的事物相对。

items.en: English took terrestrial in the 1500s, first for earthly things in theology and then for land-dwelling creatures in natural history.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入 terrestrial，最初在神学中指尘世之物，随后在博物学中指陆生生物。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the word was applied to solid, earth-like planets, giving the modern term terrestrial planet.
items.cn: 19 世纪，该词被用于有固体表面、类似地球的行星，形成现代术语 terrestrial planet。

items.en: Twentieth-century engineering used terrestrial for ground-based stations and networks, in contrast with satellite systems.
items.cn: 20 世纪的工程用语用 terrestrial 指地面站点与网络，与卫星系统相对。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the pre-Latin history of terra is unsettled, so any Indo-European root given for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：terra 在拉丁语之前的历史无定论，凡为其给出的印欧词根均属重构。

note.en: Group one separates terrestrial from same-root words naming terrain, tanks and planets, and from one look-alike from a different root; group two contrasts it with habitat terms.
note.cn: 第一组把 terrestrial 与同根却指地形、饲养箱、行星的词区分开，并辨明一个词根不同的形近词；第二组对照栖息地词语。

entries.definition: The physical surface of an area of land; it descends from Latin terrenum 'earth', so it shares terra but names ground shape, not habitat.
entries.definitionCN: 指一片土地的物质表面；源自拉丁 terrenum「土地」，与 terra 同源，但指地面形态而非栖息环境。

entries.definition: A glass container for land plants or small land animals; the -arium suffix makes it a place, not an adjective of habitat.
entries.definitionCN: 养陆生植物或小动物的玻璃容器；-arium 后缀使它指场所，而非栖息地形容词。

entries.definition: A crustal block with a geological history distinct from its neighbours; it is a technical geology term from the same terra stock.
entries.definitionCN: 地质历史与邻区不同的地壳块体；是同一 terra 词族的地质学专门术语。

entries.definition: Very good or very intense; it comes from Latin terrere 'to frighten', not terra 'earth', so the resemblance is deceptive.
entries.definitionCN: 极好的或极强烈的；来自拉丁 terrere「使害怕」而非 terra「大地」，因此形近而不同源。

entries.definition: Living or growing in water; it is the direct opposite of terrestrial in ecology.
entries.definitionCN: 在水中生活或生长的；生态学中与 terrestrial 直接相对。

entries.definition: Living in trees; it narrows the land habitat further and contrasts with ground-dwelling terrestrial species.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在树上的；它把陆地生境进一步收窄，与地栖的陆生物种相对。

entries.definition: Relating to a continent or to the interior of one; it names scale, while terrestrial names the medium.
entries.definitionCN: 与大陆或大陆内部有关的；它命名尺度，而 terrestrial 命名介质。

entries.definition: Belonging to this world rather than heaven; it is the theological and poetic cousin of terrestrial.
entries.definitionCN: 属于今生此世而非天界的；是 terrestrial 在神学与诗歌中的近亲。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real terra root, real compounds and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的 terra 词根、真实复合词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Terra is Latin for earth, and it also gives terrain, terrarium, territory and Mediterranean.
normal.cn: terra 是拉丁语的「大地」，也构成 terrain、terrarium、territory 与 Mediterranean。

normal.en: The fixed ecology pair is terrestrial / aquatic, dividing habitats by medium.
normal.cn: 生态学的固定配对是 terrestrial / aquatic，按介质划分生境。

normal.en: Extraterrestrial adds extra- 'outside' to the same adjective, so it means 'outside the earth'.
normal.cn: extraterrestrial 在同一形容词前加 extra-「之外」，意为「地球之外的」。

normal.en: Terrestrial planets are the rocky four: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars.
normal.cn: 类地行星是四颗岩石行星：水星、金星、地球与火星。

normal.en: Subterranean puts sub- 'under' before the same terra stock, meaning 'under the earth'.
normal.cn: subterranean 在同一 terra 词族前加 sub-「在下」，意为「地下的」。

abstract.en: Picture a beetle that never touches water and a fish that never touches soil, each complete in its own element.
abstract.cn: 想象一只从不沾水的甲虫与一条从不沾土的鱼，各自在自己的元素里完整无缺。

abstract.en: Picture a globe small enough to hold, with dry land painted on it as a single colour.
abstract.cn: 想象一个可以捧在手里的地球仪，干燥陆地被涂成同一种颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a radio mast rooted in soil while a satellite floats above it.
abstract.cn: 想象一根扎在土里的广播天线，而卫星在它上方漂浮。

examples.en: Terrestrial animals must conserve water in dry seasons.
examples.cn: 陆生动物在旱季必须节约用水。

examples.en: The telescope search focuses on terrestrial planets in nearby systems.
examples.cn: 这台望远镜的搜寻聚焦于邻近星系中的类地行星。

examples.en: Terrestrial carbon pools respond slowly to changes in land use.
examples.cn: 陆地碳库对土地利用变化的反应很慢。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「terra（土地）+ e（的）」——terra 是土地，terrestrial 就是「属于土地的」

root: 拉丁 terrestris「大地的」= terra「干燥陆地、大地」+ -estris（形容词后缀）；terra 的更深来源不确定，与「干燥」词根的联系仅为假说。英语 terrestrial。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move outward from soil: animals, plants, the whole planet, land as opposed to sea, rocky planets, ground-based networks, the ground layer of a forest, and land ecosystems as a global category.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从土壤向外扩展：动物、植物、整个行星、与海相对的陆地、岩石行星、地面网络、森林的地面层，以及作为全球类别的陆地生态系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: life and structures rooted in dry ground rather than water.
core.cn: 核心意象：扎根于干燥陆地而非水中的生命与设施。

branches.en: LAND-DWELLING LIFE: animals and plants are classified by the ground they occupy.
branches.cn: 陆生生命：动物与植物按所占地面被分类。

branches.en: LAND AS A REALM: the adjective widens from soil to the whole planet and to land transport.
branches.cn: 陆地领域：形容词从土壤扩展到整个行星与陆路运输。

branches.en: SOLID WORLDS: a rocky planet is land written at planetary scale.
branches.cn: 固体世界：岩石行星就是行星尺度的陆地。

branches.en: GROUND INFRASTRUCTURE: stations on land anchor broadcast networks.
branches.cn: 地面设施：陆地站点锚定广播网络。

branches.en: ECOLOGICAL DIVISIONS: ground versus canopy inside land, and land versus water globally.
branches.cn: 生态划分：陆地内部地面与树冠相对，全球范围内陆地与水相对。

intro.en: Terrestrial is a Latin adjective from terra, and that root also supports terrain, territory, terrarium and subterranean, while extra- builds its best-known opposite.
intro.cn: terrestrial 是由 terra 构成的拉丁形容词，这个词根还支撑 terrain、territory、terrarium 与 subterranean，而 extra- 构成它最知名的反义词。

latinIntro.en: Latin terra 'earth' and terrestris 'of the earth' are the direct ancestors; terrenus 'earthy' belongs to the same family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 terra「大地」与 terrestris「大地的」是直接祖形；terrenus「土质的」属于同一词族。

items.example: Terra appears in many scientific compound terms.
items.exampleCN: terra 出现在许多科学复合术语中。

items.meaning: belonging to; of the nature of

items.example: The terrestrial habitat lies above the tideline.
items.exampleCN: 陆生栖息地位于潮线之上。

items.example: The probe listens for extraterrestrial signals.
The terrain rises sharply east of the river.
items.exampleCN: 河以东的地势陡然升高。

items.example: The terrarium mimics a damp forest floor.
items.exampleCN: 饲养箱模拟湿润的森林地面。

items.example: The terrane drifted in from another plate.
items.exampleCN: 这块地体从另一板块漂移而来。

items.example: Subterranean rivers cut through the limestone.
The wolves defend a fixed territory.

definition_zh: 竞争力；竞争性
definition_en: the ability of a firm, industry or country to sell its goods and services against rivals
core_image: 一张赛跑成绩表上，同一个选手的排名年年前移，旁边的训练记录越写越厚
scene: 工厂的装配线旁，主管把本月成本表与对手的报价单并排贴在墙上。 Rising competitiveness in the region forced every plant to retool.
sceneCN: 这里 competitiveness 指「企业或地区相对对手的竞争能力」（第 1 个义项：企业在市场上胜过对手的能力）；句意为该地区竞争力的上升迫使每座工厂更新设备。图中可辨识物件：成本表、对手报价单、装配线、并排对比的墙面。

senses.title: A firm's ability to beat rivals
senses.definition: the capacity of one business to win customers and sales against its rivals
senses.definitionCN: 一家企业在与对手争夺顾客与销量时取胜的能力
senses.example: The firm's competitiveness rests on faster delivery rather than lower wages.
senses.exampleCN: 这家企业的竞争力靠的是更快的交货，而非更低的工资。
senses.why: competitive plus -ness turns an adjective of striving into the noun for the capacity itself.
senses.whyCN: competitive 加 -ness，把表示「相争」的形容词变成表示这种能力本身的名词。

senses.title: A country's export strength
senses.definition: the ability of a national economy to sell abroad and attract investment
senses.definitionCN: 一国经济在海外销售并吸引投资的能力
senses.example: The country's export competitiveness improved after the currency was adjusted.
senses.exampleCN: 汇率调整后，该国的出口竞争力有所提升。
senses.why: governments borrowed the firm-level word and scaled it up to whole economies.
senses.whyCN: 政府借用了企业层面的词，并把它放大到整个经济体。

senses.title: The strength of a cluster or region
senses.titleCN: 产业集群或区域的实力
senses.definition: the collective ability of linked firms in one place to outperform firms elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 同一地点相互关联的企业整体胜过外地企业的能力
senses.example: The cluster's competitiveness attracted suppliers from three countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个产业集群的竞争力吸引了三国的供应商。
senses.why: the unit can be a place rather than a company, because linked firms share suppliers and skills.
senses.whyCN: 计量单位可以是地点而非公司，因为相互关联的企业共享供应商与技能。

senses.title: Cost and price competitiveness
senses.definition: the ability to offer similar goods at a lower cost or price than rivals
senses.definitionCN: 以低于对手的成本或价格提供同类商品的能力
senses.example: Cheap energy gave the mills a cost competitiveness that lasted a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价能源给了这些工厂持续十年的成本竞争力。
senses.why: the phrase is often narrowed to price because the cheapest offer is the easiest advantage to measure.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法常被收窄到价格，因为最便宜的报价是最容易测量的优势。

senses.title: Strength built on productivity and innovation
senses.titleCN: 由生产率与创新支撑的竞争力
senses.definition: long-run competitive strength created by efficiency gains and new products rather than by cheap inputs
senses.definitionCN: 由效率提升与新产品而非廉价投入创造的长期竞争实力
senses.example: Innovation, not wage cuts, sustains long-run competitiveness.
senses.exampleCN: 维系长期竞争力的是创新，而非削减工资。
senses.why: economists separate this sense because cost advantage can vanish when prices or wages change.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把这一义项单列，因为成本优势会随价格或工资变化而消失。

senses.title: Advantage from exchange rates and wages
senses.titleCN: 汇率与工资带来的优势
senses.definition: a temporary edge produced by currency movements or lower labour costs
senses.definitionCN: 由汇率变动或较低劳动成本造成的暂时优势
senses.example: A strong currency hurt the sector's competitiveness overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 本币走强一夜之间削弱了该行业的竞争力。
senses.why: in trade policy the word often names price effects that no firm controls.
senses.whyCN: 在贸易政策中，这个词常指企业无法左右的价格效应。

senses.title: A rank on a competitiveness index
senses.definition: a position in a published ranking that compares economies or industries
senses.definitionCN: 在比较经济体或产业的公开排名中的位置
senses.example: The economy moved up ten places in the competitiveness index.
senses.exampleCN: 该经济体在竞争力指数上上升了十位。
senses.why: once the concept was indexed, the noun came to mean a score as well as a capacity.
senses.whyCN: 当这一概念被编成指数，这个名词也指分数，而不只是能力。

senses.title: Relative strength in any contest
senses.titleCN: 任何争夺中的相对实力
senses.definition: the degree to which any side can hold its own against competitors
senses.definitionCN: 任何一方在与对手相争时能站稳的程度
senses.example: Both teams trained for months, and their competitiveness showed in the final.
senses.exampleCN: 两队都训练了数月，决赛里显出了各自的竞争力。
senses.why: detached from trade, the noun simply measures how well a side can fight for a share.
senses.whyCN: 脱离贸易语境后，这个名词只衡量一方争夺份额的实力。

intro.en: Competitiveness is an English-built noun: the Latin verb competere gives competitive through -ive, and the native suffix -ness turns that adjective into a quality. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: competitiveness 是英语自造的名词：拉丁动词 competere 经 -ive 构成 competitive，本族后缀 -ness 再把形容词变成性质名词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Competere 'to seek together, strive jointly' joins com- 'together' to petere 'seek'. The rivalry sense was fixed in Latin before English borrowed it.
items.cn: competere「一起寻求、共同力争」把 com-「共同」接在 petere「寻求」上；相争义在英语借入前已在拉丁语中固定。

items.en: The suffix -ivus formed adjectives of tendency, as in competitivus; French -if and English -ive continue that pattern.
items.cn: 后缀 -ivus 构成表示倾向的形容词，如 competitivus；法语 -if 与英语 -ive 延续了这一模式。

items.en: Competitive entered English in the seventeenth century as an adjective for things able to contend, and later for prices and markets.
items.cn: competitive 在 17 世纪进入英语，形容能够相争的事物，后来也用于价格与市场。

items.en: The native suffix -nes, now -ness, turned adjectives into nouns of quality, as in darkness and readiness; competitiveness is a regular formation.
items.cn: 本族后缀 -nes（今 -ness）把形容词变成性质名词，如 darkness、readiness；competitiveness 是规则的构成。

items.en: Competitiveness became a policy term in the late twentieth century, when reports began ranking nations and regions by it.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期，随着报告开始据此给国家与地区排名，competitiveness 成为政策术语。

items.en: The exact first use of the noun is not recorded; nineteenth-century economics already used competitive in the modern sense. No step in the word chain is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个名词的最早用例没有确切记录；19 世纪经济学已在使用现代义的 competitive。词形链条各环节并无存疑之处。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same verb that answer a different question; group two holds related measures of performance that are not the same as the capacity itself.
note.cn: 第一组是同出那个动词、却回答不同问题的词；第二组是相关的绩效指标，与「能力」本身并不等同。

entries.definition: The process or event of rivals striving; competitiveness is a capacity, while competition is the struggle in which it shows.
entries.definitionCN: 对手相争的过程或赛事；competitiveness 是一种能力，competition 是这种能力得以显现的斗争。

entries.tag: a skill not a market edge
entries.definition: From the 'be fit for' branch of competere: a specific skill or qualification a person or firm possesses.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 competere 的「适合」一支：人或企业具备的具体技能或资格。

entries.definition: The adjective that competitiveness nominalises; it describes the side or price, not the abstract capacity.
entries.definitionCN: competitiveness 所名词化的形容词；它描述一方或价格，而非抽象能力。

entries.definition: The active participle, used for sides currently in the contest or for mutually exclusive claims.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词，用于当前正在相争的各方，或相互排斥的主张。

entries.definition: The ratio of output to input in production; it is a source of competitiveness, not the same as the ability to sell.
entries.definitionCN: 生产中产出与投入的比率；它是竞争力的来源，但不等同于销售能力。

entries.definition: The use of the least resources for a result; a firm can be efficient yet fail to sell if demand is weak.
entries.definitionCN: 用最少资源取得结果；企业可以很高效，却在需求疲弱时卖不出去。

entries.definition: One favourable condition; competitiveness is the overall capacity that such conditions support.
entries.definitionCN: 某一项有利条件；competitiveness 是这些条件所支撑的总体能力。

entries.definition: How well a firm actually did in a period; it reports results, while competitiveness predicts what results are possible.
entries.definitionCN: 企业在一段时间内的实际表现；它汇报结果，而竞争力预测可能取得什么结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: competitive + -ness: the quality of being able to strive.
normal.cn: competitive + -ness：能够相争的性质。

normal.en: The family runs compete, competition, competitor, competitive, competitively, competitiveness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 compete、competition、competitor、competitive、competitively、competitiveness。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the policy sense: international competitiveness, cost competitiveness, competitiveness index.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出政策义：国际竞争力、成本竞争力、竞争力指数。

normal.en: The word can be measured at three levels: firm, industry, country.
normal.cn: 这个词可在三个层面计量：企业、产业、国家。

normal.en: Its usual sources are productivity, innovation, skills and infrastructure.
normal.cn: 它的常见来源是生产率、创新、技能与基础设施。

abstract.en: Picture a rankings board where one name climbs a line each year.
abstract.cn: 想象一张排名板，同一个名字每年往上爬一行。

abstract.en: Picture a training log that grows thicker while the race times grow shorter.
abstract.cn: 想象训练记录越写越厚，而比赛用时越来越短。

abstract.en: Picture two factories on one river, one retooling while the other stands still.
abstract.cn: 想象同一条河边的两座工厂，一座在换设备，另一座原地不动。

examples.en: The report ranked the economy by competitiveness rather than by income.
examples.cn: 该报告按竞争力而非收入给经济体排名。

examples.en: Firms that ignore training slowly lose competitiveness.
examples.cn: 忽视培训的企业会慢慢失去竞争力。

examples.en: Currency swings can change competitiveness before any factory adjusts.
examples.cn: 汇率波动能在任何工厂作出调整之前改变竞争力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「competitive（竞争）+ ness（性质）」——能在赛场上争一争的性质 → 竞争力

root: 拉丁 competere「一起寻求、共同力争」（com- + petere「寻求」）→ 拉丁 -ivus 构成 competitivus → 英语 competitive + 本族后缀 -ness。整词为英语自造的性质名词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one capacity: a side can hold its own, and that capacity is then scaled from a firm to a country and a region, narrowed to costs, traced to productivity, tied to exchange rates, turned into a rank, and finally applied to any contest.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种能力展开：一方能站稳脚跟，这种能力再从事企业放大到国家与区域、收窄到成本、追溯到生产率、联系到汇率、变成排名，最后用于任何竞赛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a training log that thickens while the race times shorten.
core.cn: 核心意象：训练记录越写越厚，比赛用时越来越短。

branches.en: THE FIRM: the plain capacity of one business to win sales.
branches.cn: 企业：一家企业赢得销量的朴素能力。

branches.en: SCALED UP: the same capacity attributed to an economy or to a linked cluster.
branches.cn: 被放大：同一种能力被归给一个经济体或一个关联集群。

branches.en: PRICE AND CURRENCY: the cheapest offer, and the exchange-rate edge no firm controls.
branches.cn: 价格与汇率：最便宜的报价，以及企业无法左右的汇率优势。

branches.en: THE DURABLE BASE: productivity and innovation keep the capacity from evaporating.
branches.cn: 持久的基础：生产率与创新使这种能力不致蒸发。

branches.en: SCORE AND ANY CONTEST: a published rank, then the same capacity in a race or a debate.
branches.cn: 分数与任何竞赛：公开排名，以及赛跑或辩论中的同一种能力。

intro.en: The noun stacks a Latin verb, a Latin adjective suffix and a native English suffix, so each layer can be read separately.
intro.cn: 这个名词叠了一个拉丁动词、一个拉丁形容词后缀与一个英语本族后缀，因此每一层都可单独读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin competere gives compete and competition, -ivus gives competitive, and Old English -nes gives competitiveness.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 competere 提供 compete 与 competition，-ivus 提供 competitive，古英语 -nes 提供 competitiveness。

items.example: The prefix binds the striving into a shared contest.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把相争收束为共同的竞赛。

items.example: Both sides seek the same buyer.
The price is competitive in the region.
items.exampleCN: 这个价格在本地区有竞争力。

items.meaning: the quality of being able to compete
items.exampleCN: 该指数跟踪国家竞争力。

items.example: A rival opened across the street.
items.exampleCN: 街对面开了一家竞争对手。
这座老厂失去了竞争力。

items.example: The role lists five core competencies.
items.exampleCN: 该岗位列出五项核心能力。

latinEntries.meaning: to strive together; to be fit for

definition_zh: 跨学科的；学科交叉的；涉及两门以上学科的
definition_en: combining or involving two or more academic disciplines within a single project, course, team, or approach
core_image: 几间挂着不同学科牌子的教室被一条走廊打通，学生在同一张桌上拼出答案
scene: 大学实验室里，生物学家与工程师共用一张工作台。 They work on an interdisciplinary project that needs both fields.
sceneCN: 这里 interdisciplinary 是「跨学科的」（第 1 个义项：涉及两门以上学科）；句意：他们做一个需要两个领域的跨学科项目。

pos.zh: 跨学科的（用于研究、课程、团队等，指结合多门学科）
学科交叉的（用于形容方法、视角或领域本身）

derivatives.zh: 超学科的；跨学科整合的

senses.title: Combining disciplines in research
senses.definition: describing research that draws methods or data from two or more established fields to answer one question
senses.definitionCN: 描述为回答一个问题而借用两门以上成熟学科的方法或数据的研究
senses.example: The interdisciplinary study combined geology and archaeology to date the eruption.
senses.exampleCN: 这项跨学科研究结合地质学与考古学来确定喷发年代。
senses.why: Interdisciplinary is inter- 'between' plus disciplinary, from Latin disciplina 'instruction, knowledge'. The adjective asserts that a question sits between fields — no single discipline owns it.
senses.whyCN: interdisciplinary 是 inter-“在……之间”加 disciplinary，而后者源自拉丁语 disciplina“教导、知识”。这个形容词主张某个问题处在学科之间——没有哪一门学科独占它。

senses.title: Spanning disciplines in teaching
senses.definition: describing a course or curriculum that teaches content from several fields in one programme
senses.definitionCN: 描述在一门课程或培养方案中教授多个领域内容的课程
senses.example: The university offers an interdisciplinary major in climate and public policy.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学开设气候与公共政策方向的跨学科专业。
senses.why: Education uses the adjective to describe structure: one timetable, several departments. The word signals that students are expected to move between vocabularies, not to master one.
senses.whyCN: 教育领域用这个形容词描述结构：一张课表，几个院系。这个词表明学生要在不同词汇体系之间移动，而不是精通其中一门。

senses.title: Working across disciplines in a team
senses.definition: describing a group whose members are trained in different fields and share a task
senses.definitionCN: 描述成员受训于不同领域并共担任务的团队
senses.example: An interdisciplinary team of engineers and physicians designed the device.
senses.exampleCN: 由工程师与医生组成的跨学科团队设计了这台设备。
senses.why: Here the adjective describes people rather than knowledge: the team's strength is that no member can read the whole problem alone. The prefix marks the seam between specialisms.
senses.whyCN: 这里的形容词描述人而不是知识：团队的力量在于没有哪个成员能独自读懂整个问题。前缀标记的正是专业之间的接缝。

senses.title: Borrowing methods across fields
senses.definition: describing an approach that applies the tools or models of one field to the problems of another
senses.definitionCN: 描述把一个领域的工具或模型用于另一个领域问题的做法
senses.example: The paper takes an interdisciplinary approach, using network theory to read historical records.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文采用跨学科方法，用网络理论解读历史记录。
senses.why: The adjective often attaches to 'approach' or 'method', where the borrowing is deliberate rather than accidental. A method becomes interdisciplinary when its assumptions are imported along with its techniques.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词常修饰 approach 或 method，那里的借用是有意的而非偶然。当一套方法的假设连同技术一起被引入时，它就变成跨学科的。

senses.title: Naming an emerging field
senses.definition: describing a field that exists only where two or more disciplines overlap, such as bioinformatics
senses.definitionCN: 描述仅在两门或更多学科交叠处存在的领域，如生物信息学
senses.example: Bioinformatics is an interdisciplinary field born from biology and computer science.
senses.exampleCN: 生物信息学是由生物学与计算机科学孕育出的交叉学科领域。
senses.why: When a hybrid field matures, the adjective becomes part of its name. The word then no longer describes a project but a territory that belongs to no single department.
senses.whyCN: 当一个杂交领域成熟时，这个形容词就成为它名字的一部分。此时这个词不再描述一个项目，而描述一块不属于任何单一院系的领地。

senses.title: Institutional cross-department arrangement
senses.definition: describing centres, institutes, or programmes set up to connect departments that normally work apart
senses.definitionCN: 描述为连接通常各自为政的院系而设立的中心、研究所或项目
senses.example: The interdisciplinary centre reports to three faculties at once.
senses.exampleCN: 这个跨学科中心同时向三个学院汇报。
senses.why: Universities invented such units to solve an administrative problem: budgets and appointments sit inside departments, while problems do not. The word names the exception built to cross those walls.
senses.whyCN: 大学发明这类单位是为了解决一个管理难题：预算与人事都在院系内部，而问题不在。这个词命名的是为穿越这些墙而建的例外。

senses.title: An interdisciplinary perspective
senses.definition: describing an analytical view that deliberately holds several disciplinary framings at once
senses.definitionCN: 描述有意同时持有多种学科框架的分析视角
senses.example: Her interdisciplinary reading of the novel draws on economics and theology.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这部小说的跨学科解读借用了经济学与神学。
senses.why: This sense is about seeing, not organising: the analyst keeps two frames active and lets them correct each other. The prefix becomes a way of preventing a single frame from claiming the whole truth.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项关乎“看”，而非“组织”：分析者让两个框架同时工作，并让它们互相纠正。前缀由此成为一种手段，防止单一框架宣称掌握全部真相。

senses.title: Interdisciplinary in a degree or publication
senses.titleCN: 学位或成果的跨学科属性
senses.definition: describing a thesis, journal, or degree formally labelled as spanning more than one discipline
senses.definitionCN: 描述被正式标注为横跨一门以上学科的论文、期刊或学位
senses.example: The dissertation was accepted as interdisciplinary work by a joint committee.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文被联合委员会接受为跨学科成果。
senses.why: Institutions need labels for evaluation: a joint committee, a mixed methodology, a shared credit. The adjective here is a classification with real consequences for funding and hiring.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要用于评估的标签：联合委员会、混合方法、共享学分。这里的形容词是一种分类，对经费与聘任有实际后果。

intro.en: Interdisciplinary is inter- 'between' plus disciplinary, from Latin disciplina 'teaching, knowledge', itself from discipulus 'pupil' and discere 'to learn'. The compound is a twentieth-century English coinage, not a Latin word.
intro.cn: interdisciplinary 是 inter-“在……之间”加 disciplinary，后者源自拉丁语 disciplina“教导、知识”，而 disciplina 又来自 discipulus“学生”与 discere“学习”。这个复合词是 20 世纪英语的创造，不是拉丁语词。

items.en: Latin discere meant 'to learn'; discipulus 'pupil' and disciplina 'instruction, field of knowledge' came from it. Disciplina already carried both meanings that English still keeps: training and a branch of study.
items.cn: 拉丁语 discere 意为“学习”；discipulus“学生”与 disciplina“教导、知识领域”由此而来。disciplina 已经带有英语仍保留的两重含义：训练与一门学问。

items.en: English discipline entered through Old French with the senses 'instruction', 'a branch of learning', and 'correction'. The punitive sense and the academic sense grew side by side from the same idea of training.
items.cn: 英语 discipline 经古法语进入，义为“教导”“一门学问”“纠正”。惩罚义与学术义从同一个“训练”观念中并肩生长出来。

items.en: The modern research university organized knowledge into departments, and 'discipline' became the word for those units. Boundaries were the point: each field had its own methods and journals.
items.cn: 现代研究型大学把知识组织成系科，discipline 于是成为这些单位的名称。边界正是关键：每个领域有自己的方法与期刊。

items.en: Interdisciplinary is generally dated to the 1920s and 1930s, when foundations and universities began funding work that crossed departments. The exact first use is uncertain, but the coinage is not in doubt.
items.cn: interdisciplinary 一般被认为产生于 1920 至 1930 年代，当时基金会与大学开始资助跨越院系的工作。确切首次使用来源不确定，但属新造词这一点无疑。

items.en: Cold War research projects, area studies, and later environmental science made cross-department work normal. The adjective moved from describing exceptions to naming whole programmes and fields.
items.cn: 冷战时期的研究项目、区域研究以及后来的环境科学使跨系工作成为常态。这个形容词从描述例外，转为命名整个项目与领域。

items.en: Today the word sits beside multidisciplinary and transdisciplinary, each marking a different depth of integration. Interdisciplinary usually means fields cooperate on a shared question while keeping their methods.
items.cn: 今天这个词与 multidisciplinary、transdisciplinary 并列，各自标记不同的整合深度。interdisciplinary 通常指各领域围绕共同问题合作，同时保留各自的方法。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the multi-, cross-, and trans- forms, which differ in how deeply the disciplines are integrated; the near-meaning group separates words for combined and cooperative work.
note.cn: 形近组区分 multi-、cross-、trans- 三种形式，它们的学科整合深度不同；近义组区分表示“结合”与“合作”的词。

entries.definition: involving several disciplines placed next to each other. Multi- 'many' suggests parallel contributions rather than a single fused method, which is weaker integration than interdisciplinary.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及多门学科并置。multi-“多”暗示各学科平行贡献，而不是融合成一套方法，整合程度比 interdisciplinary 弱。

entries.definition: crossing disciplinary boundaries so thoroughly that a new framework is created. Trans- 'across, beyond' marks deeper integration than interdisciplinary.
entries.definitionCN: 如此彻底地穿越学科边界，以致产生新框架。trans-“越过、之外”标记比 interdisciplinary 更深的整合。

entries.definition: relating to a discipline of study, or to correction and punishment. Without inter- it stays inside one field or refers to rules.
entries.definitionCN: 与某一学科有关的，或与惩戒有关的。没有 inter- 时，它仍在一门学科之内，或指规则。

entries.definition: working across the boundaries of disciplines. It is close to interdisciplinary but more often describes a single crossing, such as a team drawn from two departments.
entries.definitionCN: 跨越学科边界工作。它接近 interdisciplinary，但更常描述单次跨越，例如由两个院系组成的团队。

entries.definition: combined into a working whole. It describes the outcome, while interdisciplinary describes the range of fields involved.
entries.definitionCN: 结合成一个可运转的整体。它描述结果，而 interdisciplinary 描述所涉领域的范围。

entries.definition: involving people working together. It names the cooperation itself, not the academic disciplines of the participants.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及人们一起工作的。它命名合作本身，而不是参与者的学科归属。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: inter- 'between' + disciplina 'knowledge', the department walls of the modern university, and the standard phrases interdisciplinary research and interdisciplinary team.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：inter-“在……之间”+ disciplina“知识”、现代大学的院系之墙，以及 interdisciplinary research、interdisciplinary team 等标准说法。

normal.en: inter- means 'between': interdisciplinary work happens in the corridor between two departments, not in either office.
normal.cn: inter- 意为“在……之间”：跨学科工作发生在两个院系之间的走廊里，而不在任何一间办公室。

normal.en: discipline means both 'a field of study' and 'training', so the word is about trained fields meeting.
normal.cn: discipline 既指“一门学问”，也指“训练”，所以这个词讲的是受过训练的领域相遇。

normal.en: A bioinformatics lab is the clearest picture: half computer science, half biology, one room.
normal.cn: 生物信息学实验室是最清楚的画面：一半计算机科学，一半生物学，同一间屋子。

normal.en: If two fields merely sit side by side, say multidisciplinary; if they fuse, say interdisciplinary.
normal.cn: 两门学科只是并排放着，就用 multidisciplinary；如果融合了，就用 interdisciplinary。

normal.en: An interdisciplinary degree is judged by a joint committee because no single department owns it.
normal.cn: 跨学科学位由联合委员会评定，因为没有哪个院系独占它。

abstract.en: The word does not mean 'knowing a little of everything'; it means holding two rigorous methods at once.
abstract.cn: 这个词不是“什么都懂一点”；它指同时持有两套严谨的方法。

abstract.en: Its value is the seam: at the boundary each discipline is forced to explain assumptions it normally hides.
abstract.cn: 它的价值在接缝处：在边界上，每门学科都被迫解释它平时藏起来的假设。

abstract.en: Departments organize knowledge; interdisciplinary work organizes questions, and questions do not respect walls.
abstract.cn: 院系组织知识；跨学科工作组织问题，而问题不尊重围墙。

examples.en: The interdisciplinary project brought together geologists and historians.
examples.cn: 这个跨学科项目把地质学家与历史学家聚到一起。

examples.en: She chose an interdisciplinary major combining economics and environmental science.
examples.cn: 她选择了结合经济学与环境科学的跨学科专业。

examples.en: Interdisciplinary research is often judged by committees drawn from several faculties.
examples.cn: 跨学科研究常由来自多个学院的委员会评审。

dict_mnemonic.text: “因它来，弟子扑来呢”——它一来，几门学科的弟子都扑到一张桌子上 → interdisciplinary 跨学科的

root: inter-（在……之间）+ 拉丁语 discere“学习”/discipulus“学生”/disciplina“教导、学问”+ -ary；字面义“处于学科之间的”，核心是“多门学科围绕同一问题合作”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of interdisciplinary all place a question, course, team, method, field, centre, reading, or degree between established disciplines. The word marks a seam rather than a mixture: fields cooperate while keeping their own standards.
sensesIntro.cn: interdisciplinary 的八个义项都把某个问题、课程、团队、方法、领域、中心、解读或学位放在成熟学科之间。这个词标记的是一条接缝，而不是一锅混合：各领域合作，同时保留各自的标准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several classrooms with different subject signs joined by one corridor, all working at one table.
core.cn: 核心意象：几间挂着不同学科牌子的教室由一条走廊连通，共用一张桌子工作。

branches.en: METHOD: research and analysis borrow tools across a boundary while keeping each field's assumptions visible.
branches.cn: 方法：研究与分析跨边界借用工具，同时让每个领域的假设保持可见。

branches.en: INSTITUTION: courses, degrees, and joint committees are formal arrangements for crossing walls.
branches.cn: 制度：课程、学位与联合委员会是为穿墙而设的正式安排。

branches.en: PEOPLE: a team is interdisciplinary when no member can read the whole problem alone.
branches.cn: 人：当没有成员能独自读懂整个问题时，团队就是跨学科的。

branches.en: FIELD: a hybrid subject such as bioinformatics exists only in the overlap.
branches.cn: 领域：生物信息学这类杂交学科只存在于交叠处。

branches.en: PERSPECTIVE: centres and cross-readings keep two frames active so neither claims the whole truth.
branches.cn: 视角：中心与交叉解读让两个框架同时工作，使任何一方都不能宣称掌握全部真相。

intro.en: Interdisciplinary is inter- + disciplinary, and disciplinary is discipline + -ary. Discipline comes from Latin disciplina. The affix set contrasts the multi-, cross-, and trans- variants with the base word.
intro.cn: interdisciplinary 是 inter- + disciplinary，而 disciplinary 是 discipline + -ary。discipline 源自拉丁语 disciplina。词缀组把 multi-、cross-、trans- 各变体与基础词对照起来。

latinIntro.en: Latin disciplina 'instruction, knowledge' derives from discipulus 'pupil', from discere 'to learn'. The older link to docere 'to teach' is generally accepted but the exact derivation is debated, so it is marked as probable rather than certain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 disciplina“教导、知识”源自 discipulus“学生”，而 discipulus 又来自 discere“学习”。它与 docere“教”的更早关联一般被认为是成立的，但确切派生过程有争议，因此标为“一般认为”而非确定。

items.meaning: spanning more than one field of study
items.exampleCN: 这个中心开展跨学科研究。

items.meaning: a field of study; controlled training
items.meaningCN: 学科；纪律；训练（直接借自拉丁名词）
items.exampleCN: 历史学是一门要求很高的学科。

items.meaning: relating to a field or to correction
items.meaningCN: 学科的；纪律的（-ary 构成形容词）
items.exampleCN: 这篇论文跨越学科界线。

items.meaningCN: 严格执行纪律者（-arian 表人）
items.example: The coach was a strict disciplinarian.
items.exampleCN: 这位教练严格执行纪律。

items.meaning: the quality of belonging to a discipline
items.meaningCN: 学科性（-ity 构成抽象名词）
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章质疑传统的学科性。

items.meaning: using several disciplines side by side
items.example: A multidisciplinary panel reviewed the plan.
items.exampleCN: 一个多学科小组评审了这项方案。

items.meaning: crossing disciplines to build a new frame
items.exampleCN: 超学科工作消解旧的边界。
这笔资助支持交叉学科团队。

items.meaningCN: 缺乏训练的；无纪律的（un- 表否定）
items.example: The undisciplined method produced noisy data.
items.exampleCN: 缺乏规范的方法产生了嘈杂的数据。

latinEntries.meaning: instruction, knowledge, a branch of study
teacher; the root is related but the exact path is debated
latinEntries.meaningCN: 教师；词根与 discere 相关，但确切派生路径有争议（来源不确定）

definition_zh: 体力劳动者；雇工；靠出力换工资的人
definition_en: a person who does physical work, especially for wages and without special training
core_image: 码头跳板上，一个肩扛麻袋的人慢慢走向仓库，掌心全是粗茧
scene: 码头清晨，一排工人扛着麻袋从跳板走向货舱，脚边是散落的谷粒。 A laborer hauled sacks of grain from the barge to the warehouse all morning.
sceneCN: 这里 laborer 指「以体力换工资的劳动者」（第 1 个义项：从事体力劳动并领取工资的人）；句意为一名搬运工整个上午都在把粮袋从驳船扛到仓库。图中可辨识物件：跳板、麻袋、驳船、仓库门、掌心的茧。

pos.zh: 体力劳动者；雇工（美式拼写，英式作 labourer）

senses.title: A person who works with the body for wages
senses.titleCN: 以体力劳动换取工资的人
senses.definition: someone whose work is mainly physical and who is paid for it by another
senses.definitionCN: 主要靠体力干活、并由他人支付报酬的人
senses.example: A laborer hauled sacks of grain from the barge to the warehouse all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 一名搬运工整个上午都在把粮袋从驳船扛到仓库。
senses.why: The root names toil itself rather than a trade, so the person is defined by effort and by being paid for it.
senses.whyCN: 词根命名的是「辛苦劳作」本身而非某门手艺，因此这个人由出力、并由他人付酬来界定。

senses.title: A worker on a site or in a plant
senses.titleCN: 工地或厂区里的体力工人
senses.definition: a worker doing digging, lifting, carrying or cleaning on a building site or in a factory
senses.definitionCN: 在建筑工地或工厂里从事挖掘、搬运、扛抬或清理的工人
senses.example: Fifty laborers cleared the rubble before the crane arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 吊车到场之前，五十名工人清理了瓦砾。
senses.why: The word covers the tasks that need strength and endurance more than training, which is exactly the work found on a site.
senses.whyCN: 这个词涵盖的是更需要力气与耐力、而非专门训练的任务，正是工地上的活。

senses.title: A worker paid by the day
senses.definition: a worker hired for short periods and paid for each day worked
senses.definitionCN: 按短期雇用、按实际出工的天数领钱的人
senses.example: The foreman hired twenty laborers at dawn and paid them at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 工头天亮时雇了二十名短工，天黑时结清工钱。
senses.why: Day payment is the oldest arrangement for work that needs no contract, and the plain word for toil fits that arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 按日付酬是无需合同的工作最古老的安排，而指称「辛苦劳作」的朴素词正合这种安排。

senses.title: A farmhand
senses.definition: a person hired to do seasonal or general work on a farm
senses.definitionCN: 受雇在农场上做季节性杂活的人
senses.example: Two laborers stayed through the harvest and slept in the barn loft.
senses.exampleCN: 两名帮工一直干到收完庄稼，睡在谷仓的阁楼上。
senses.why: Farm work is the historical home of wage toil, so the generic word settled there first and is still used for it.
senses.whyCN: 农活是雇佣劳作的历史故乡，因此这个泛称最早在那里落定，至今仍用于农活。

senses.title: A worker whose contribution is mainly strength
senses.titleCN: 主要靠力气而非技能的劳动者
senses.definition: used to contrast such a worker with a trained or skilled one
senses.definitionCN: 用于把这类劳动者与受过训练或有专门技术的劳动者相对照
senses.example: The crew split into skilled hands and laborers, and the pay followed that line.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍分成技工与力工，工钱也按这条线分开。
senses.why: The word carries no hint of a craft, so it naturally serves as the unmarked term on the other side of 'skilled'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不带任何手艺的意味，因此自然充当「有技术」一侧之外的默认说法。

senses.title: Anyone bearing heavy physical toil
senses.titleCN: 承受繁重体力负担的人
senses.definition: used more broadly, and often in writing, of a person under exhausting physical effort
senses.definitionCN: 较宽泛地、常见于书面语，指承受令人疲惫的体力重负的人
senses.example: The poet pictured the laborer bent under a load no machine would lift.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人想象那个劳动者弯着腰，扛着机器也吊不起的重物。
senses.why: Because the root means hardship as much as work, the word can leave the workplace and name the burden itself.
senses.whyCN: 既因词根兼指「艰辛」与「劳作」，这个词就能离开工作场所，直接指称那份重负。

senses.title: The labouring class in older economic writing
senses.titleCN: 旧经济学著作中的劳动者阶级
senses.definition: a collective label used in older political economy for those who live by selling physical effort
senses.definitionCN: 旧政治经济学中用来统称靠出卖体力为生者的集体标签
senses.example: The old tract counted the laborer among the three orders of society.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧论著把劳动者算作社会三个等级之一。
senses.why: Once the word was generalized, it could stand for a whole order of society, and economic writers used it that way.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一旦被泛化，就能代表整个社会等级，经济学者便如此使用它。

senses.title: Someone who works for another rather than for himself
senses.titleCN: 为他人而非为自己干活的人
senses.definition: used to mark the subordinate side of a working relation
senses.definitionCN: 用以标出劳动关系中处于从属的一方
senses.example: A laborer sells hours; an owner sells what those hours produce.
senses.exampleCN: 劳动者出卖的是钟点，所有者出卖的是那些钟点产出的东西。
senses.why: The absence of ownership in the word's meaning makes it a natural marker of the hired side of a relation.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的含义里没有「所有权」，使它自然成为雇佣关系中被雇一方的标记。

intro.en: Laborer joins Latin labor 'toil, hardship' to the native agent suffix -er. The noun came into English through Anglo-French, and the two spellings laborer and labourer split in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: laborer 由拉丁 labor「辛劳、艰苦」加英语本族施事后缀 -er 构成。这个名词经盎格鲁-法语进入英语，laborer 与 labourer 两种拼写在 19 世纪分家。年代均为约数。

items.en: Labor, laboris named toil, exertion and hardship rather than a particular craft, which is why the word never narrows to one trade.
items.cn: labor（属格 laboris）指辛劳、出力与艰苦，而非某一门手艺，因此这个词从未收窄到单一工种。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of labor is not established. A link to labare 'to totter, give way' has been suggested, picturing toil as a load that makes the body sway, but it remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定：labor 的更早来源未得证明。有人提出它与 labare「摇晃、支撑不住」相关，把辛劳想成压得身体打晃的重负，但这仍只是假说。

items.en: Middle English took the noun through Anglo-French, where labour already meant both the effort and the work done.
items.cn: 中古英语经盎格鲁-法语借入这个名词，那里的 labour 已兼指出力与所干的活。

items.en: The agent suffix -er is native English, from Old English -ere, so laborer is a Latin noun fitted with an English ending.
items.cn: 施事后缀 -er 是英语本族成分，出自古英语 -ere，因此 laborer 是一个拉丁名词套上了英语词尾。

items.en: American usage keeps laborer and labor; British usage keeps labourer and labour, a division that settled in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 美式用法保留 laborer 与 labor，英式用法保留 labourer 与 labour，这一分歧在 19 世纪定型。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest use of the word for a wage earner rather than for any toiling person is not firmly dated, and sources differ by more than a century.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个词最早何时专指领工资者而非泛指任何出力的人，没有可靠年代，各家说法相差百余年。

note.en: The first group holds words that look or sound close but mark a different kind of worker; the second holds near synonyms that differ in skill, contract or tone.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或音近、却指另一类劳动者的词；第二组是技能、合同形式或语气上有差别的近义词。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the same noun; nothing in meaning changes.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个名词的英式拼写，含义没有任何变化。

entries.definition: Names the work or the effort, or the verb 'to work'; it does not name a person.
entries.definitionCN: 指劳动或出力，或作动词「干活」；不指人。

entries.definition: From Latin laborare 'to work' in its medieval sense of a place for work, but the modern word means a research room, not a worker.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 laborare「工作」在中世纪指干活之处，但现代词义是研究实验室，不是劳动者。

entries.definition: Built on com- 'together' plus laborare, so it means a fellow worker on a project, not a manual wage earner.
entries.definitionCN: 由 com-「共同」加 laborare 构成，指项目上的合作者，而非体力雇工。

entries.definition: The plain word for anyone who works, including office staff; it says nothing about physical effort.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何工作者的中性词，包括办公室人员；不含体力成分。

entries.definition: A manual worker, usually one with a trade and often male; it implies craft where laborer implies none.
entries.definitionCN: 手工劳动者，通常有手艺且多为男性；它含手艺意味，而 laborer 不含。

entries.definition: Informal for a member of a work crew, as in farm hand or deck hand; it is tied to a particular setting.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中指作业队的一员，如农场帮工、甲板水手；与特定场景绑定。

entries.definition: Defined by being hired, not by the kind of work; a clerk is an employee but not a laborer.
entries.definitionCN: 以受雇界定，而非以工作性质界定；职员是雇员却不是体力劳动者。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real relatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的同族词与真实的固定说法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin labor means toil and hardship, and the English ending -er marks the person who bears it.
normal.cn: 拉丁 labor 意为辛劳与艰苦，英语词尾 -er 标出承担它的人。

normal.en: The family runs labor, laborer, laborious, laboriously.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 labor、laborer、laborious、laboriously。

normal.en: Fixed phrases place the word: day laborer, farm laborer, unskilled laborer.
normal.cn: 固定说法给出位置：按日雇工、农业雇工、非技术体力工。

normal.en: The British spelling doubles the u: labourer.
normal.cn: 英式拼写多一个 u：labourer。

normal.en: Laborer sits opposite skilled in hiring talk, which shows the word carries no craft.
normal.cn: 在招工话语里 laborer 与 skilled 相对，可见这个词不含手艺意味。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of hands as the only tool a person owns.
abstract.cn: 想象一双手就是一个人全部的工具。

abstract.en: Picture a scale where effort sits on one pan and wages on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，一头放着力气，一头放着工钱。

abstract.en: Picture a body bent under a load that no crane would be asked to lift.
abstract.cn: 想象一副被重物压弯的身板，那重量不会有人叫吊车去吊。

examples.en: The contractor took on thirty laborers for the summer.
examples.cn: 承包商夏天招了三十名体力工。

examples.en: A laborer on the night shift earns less than the machine operator beside him.
examples.cn: 夜班搬运工挣得比旁边的机器操作工少。

examples.en: The novel follows a farm laborer who never learns to read.
examples.cn: 这部小说写一个始终没学会识字的农业帮工。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累（lab）的人（-er）」——靠出力换工资 → 体力劳动者

root: 拉丁 labor「辛劳、艰苦」+ 英语本族施事后缀 -er。labor 的更早来源不确定，与 labare「摇晃、支撑不住」的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from one figure, a person whose strength is for sale, and then move outward: the site, the daily wage, the farm, the missing craft, the burden itself, a class label and finally the hired side of a relation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个人物出发——一个把力气拿去卖的人——再向外扩展：工地、日薪、农场、缺失的手艺、重负本身、阶级标签，最后是雇佣关系中被雇的一方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pair of calloused hands on a gangplank, carrying a load for someone else's account.
core.cn: 核心意象：跳板上的一双粗手，替别人的账目扛着货。

branches.en: EFFORT FOR HIRE: the person is defined by body work first, and then by the place where that work is done.
branches.cn: 以力换酬：这个人先由体力活界定，再由干这活的地点界定。

branches.en: SHORT HIRE: a daily wage and a seasonal farm stint are the two oldest forms of the arrangement.
branches.cn: 短期雇佣：日薪与农场季节工是这种安排最古老的两种形态。

branches.en: NO CRAFT, THEN THE BURDEN: once skill is absent, the word can name the load rather than the job.
branches.cn: 无手艺，进而指重负：一旦技能缺席，这个词便可指负担而非职业。

branches.en: CLASS LABEL: political economy generalized the figure into a whole order of society.
branches.cn: 阶级标签：政治经济学把这一形象泛化为整个社会等级。

branches.en: HIRED SIDE: the last sense is relational, naming whoever works for another's account.
branches.cn: 受雇一方：最后一个义项是关系性的，指为他人账目干活的人。

intro.en: The word is a Latin noun of toil with a native English ending, so the root and the ending each build their own set of English words.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个表辛劳的拉丁名词配上英语本族词尾，因此词根与词尾各自构成一批英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin labor and its verb laborare give labor, laborious, elaborate, collaborate and laboratory; the ending -er marks the person who performs the action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 labor 及其动词 laborare 衍生 labor、laborious、elaborate、collaborate 与 laboratory；词尾 -er 标出动作的执行者。

items.example: The noun names effort before it names a job.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词先指出力，再指职业。

items.structure: laborare, laboravi, laboratum (Latin verb, first conjugation)
items.example: The verb supplied the international family of labour words.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供了国际通行的 labor 词族。

items.structure: -er (native English agent suffix, from Old English -ere)
items.example: The ending turns an activity into a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把一项活动变成一个人。

items.example: His labored breathing worried the nurse.
items.exampleCN: 他吃力的呼吸让护士担心。

items.example: The laborious climb took six hours.

definition_zh: 墓室；（陵墓内的）棺室
definition_en: a room built underground or inside a tomb, where a body or coffin is placed
core_image: 石砌的小房间埋在地底，门口被整块石板封住，屋里只放一具棺与几件随身器物
scene: 石阶向下通向一间石砌小屋，门口被整块石板封住，屋里只摆着一具棺。 Stone steps led down to a sealed burial chamber that held a single coffin.
sceneCN: 这里 burial chamber 指「墓穴内用来安放棺椁的石室」（第 1 个义项：墓中专设的置棺空间）；句意为石阶向下通向一间封住的墓室，里面只放着一具棺。可辨识物件：石阶、石板门、石室、棺。
