senses.title: A room for a coffin
senses.definition: a room inside a tomb where a coffin or body is placed
senses.definitionCN: 墓穴或陵墓内部用来放置棺木或遗体的空间
senses.example: The coffin was carried into the burial chamber before the slab was closed.
senses.exampleCN: 石板封上之前，棺木被抬进墓室。
senses.why: The phrase simply joins the act of burying to the room that receives the body, so the name describes the room's function.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把「埋葬」这个动作与承接遗体的「房间」直接连在一起，名称说明的就是房间的用途。

senses.title: The underground part of a grave
senses.definition: the covered lower space dug beneath a grave, distinct from the shaft above
senses.definitionCN: 坟墓下方被封住的空间，与上方的竖井部分相区别
senses.example: The shaft was filled with rubble, but the burial chamber beneath it stayed dry.
senses.exampleCN: 竖井被碎石填满，但下面的墓室保持干燥。
senses.why: Once burials were cut as shafts with a side room, the room needed its own name.
senses.whyCN: 当墓葬被挖成带侧室的竖井后，侧室就需要一个自己的名称。

senses.title: An inner room of a royal tomb
senses.definition: one of the inner rooms of a large royal or noble tomb
senses.definitionCN: 大型王室或贵族陵墓内部的一个房间
senses.example: The royal burial chamber held a stone sarcophagus and a chest of ornaments.
senses.exampleCN: 王室墓室里放着一具石棺和一只装首饰的箱子。
senses.why: Large tombs divide into several rooms, and the one that holds the principal body keeps the phrase.
senses.whyCN: 大型陵墓分成若干房间，其中安放主要遗体的那一间保留了这个称呼。

senses.title: A room cut into rock
senses.definition: a chamber excavated directly into bedrock rather than built of masonry
senses.definitionCN: 直接在基岩中凿出、而非用石块砌成的墓室
senses.example: Workers cut the rock-cut burial chamber from the cliff in a single season.
senses.exampleCN: 工匠用一个季节就从崖壁上凿出了这间岩凿墓室。
senses.why: Rock-cut tombs reuse the phrase because the room, not the material, defines it.
senses.whyCN: 岩凿墓沿用这个短语，因为定义它的是「室」这一空间，而非建筑材料。

senses.title: The archaeological unit
senses.definition: the recorded room of a tomb as a distinct unit of excavation and study
senses.definitionCN: 作为独立发掘与研究单元的墓葬房间
senses.example: Each burial chamber on the site was numbered and photographed in plan.
senses.exampleCN: 遗址中的每一间墓室都被编号并拍摄了平面照片。
senses.why: Archaeology treats the room as a unit because its contents and walls can be recorded separately.
senses.whyCN: 考古学把「室」当作单元，因为它的随葬品与四壁可以分别记录。

senses.title: A room for grave goods
senses.definition: a side room or recess holding objects buried with the dead
senses.definitionCN: 存放随葬器物的侧室或壁龛
senses.example: The smaller burial chamber was stacked with jars and model boats.
senses.exampleCN: 较小的那间墓室堆满了陶罐与模型船。
senses.why: Side chambers were often made for offerings rather than for the body, and the phrase covers both.
senses.whyCN: 侧室常为放置供品而非安放遗体而建，这个短语两者都能指。

senses.title: A family vault
senses.definition: a chamber used by one family for several burials over time
senses.definitionCN: 一个家族长期使用、先后安葬多人的墓室
senses.example: Three generations were laid in the same burial chamber beneath the chapel.
senses.exampleCN: 三代人都被安放在礼拜堂下的同一间墓室里。
senses.why: When a room is reopened for later burials, the phrase shifts from a single event to a family institution.
senses.whyCN: 当一间墓室为后续安葬反复开启，这个短语就从单次事件转为家族制度。

senses.title: A sealed space in metaphor
senses.definition: any closed space treated as if it held something preserved and hidden
senses.definitionCN: 任何被当作封存、藏匿之处的封闭空间
senses.example: The archive is a burial chamber of forgotten files.
senses.exampleCN: 那座档案库是一座封存被遗忘文件的墓室。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps two features of the literal room: it is closed, and what is inside is not meant to be disturbed.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留字面墓室的两个特征：它是封闭的，里面的东西不打算被打扰。

intro.en: Burial chamber joins an Old English burial word to a Latin-derived room word; the compound itself is a modern descriptive label. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: burial chamber 把古英语的「埋葬」词与拉丁来源的「房间」词连在一起，这个复合词本身是近代的描述性称名。年代均为约数。

items.en: Old English byrgan meant 'to bury, inter', from Proto-Germanic burjan 'to raise a mound', a word related to berg 'hill or mound'.
items.cn: 古英语 byrgan 意为「埋葬、安葬」，源自原始日耳曼语 burjan「堆起土丘」，与 berg「山丘、土堆」同族。

items.en: The noun for a tomb was byrgels; Middle English reshaped it as buriel, and later speakers refashioned it as bury plus -al.
items.cn: 指坟墓的名词是 byrgels；中古英语把它改作 buriel，后来又说者按 bury 加 -al 重新构形。

items.en: Greek kamara 'vaulted cover' gave Latin camera 'vaulted room', which passed through Old French chambre into English chamber.
items.cn: 希腊 kamara「拱顶盖」产生拉丁 camera「拱顶房间」，再经古法语 chambre 进入英语 chamber。

items.en: English joins two existing nouns to name the room that receives a body; no single coining date is recorded for the phrase.
items.cn: 英语把两个已有名词连起来，指承接遗体的房间；这个短语没有单一可考的首创年代。

items.en: From the nineteenth century excavated tombs were described room by room, and burial chamber became a standard unit of description.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，发掘的墓葬按房间逐一描述，burial chamber 成为标准的描述单元。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the phrase has no recorded first citation, and whether byrgan came from a mound word or from a protecting word is disputed, so both accounts remain hypotheses.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：该短语没有可考的最早书证；byrgan 究竟出自「土丘」还是「保护」一词仍有争议，两种说法都只是假说。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like chamber or burial but come from elsewhere; group two holds other rooms and structures made for the dead.
note.cn: 第一组是与 chamber、burial 形近却另有来历的词；第二组是为死者造的其他房间与建筑。

entries.definition: Latin camera 'vaulted room' also gave camera; chamber and camera are doublets, not unrelated words.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁 camera「拱顶房间」也产生 camera；chamber 与 camera 是同源异形词，并非无关。

entries.definition: From Latin camur 'curved', describing a slight upward curve in a road or wing.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 camur「弯曲的」，指路面或机翼的轻微上拱。

entries.definition: From French chanfrein 'bevel', with no link to Latin camera or to a room.
entries.definitionCN: 来自法语 chanfrein「斜切」，与拉丁 camera 或房间均无关联。

entries.definition: A different burial word from Greek 'sleeping place'; it names the ground, not the inner room.
entries.definitionCN: 另一个指墓地的词，来自希腊语「安睡之处」；它指整片土地，而非内部房间。

entries.definition: The whole built structure for the dead, of which the chamber is one part.
entries.definitionCN: 为死者建造的整体建筑，墓室只是其中一部分。

entries.definition: An underground vault, especially beneath a church, from Greek kryptos 'hidden'.
entries.definitionCN: 地下拱室，尤指教堂之下，来自希腊 kryptos「隐藏的」。

entries.definition: An arched or domed burial space, named for its curved roof.
entries.definitionCN: 拱形或穹顶的墓葬空间，以其弧状顶盖得名。

entries.definition: A large monumental tomb building, from the name of Mausolus of Caria.
entries.definitionCN: 大型纪念性陵墓建筑，得名于卡里亚的摩索拉斯。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real archaeology terms and the genuine doublet camera.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词成分、真实考古术语，以及真实存在的同源异形词 camera。

normal.en: Old English byrgan 'to bury' is related to berg 'hill', the image of a raised mound.
normal.cn: 古英语 byrgan「埋葬」与 berg「山丘」同族，意象是堆起的土丘。

normal.en: Chamber and camera are doublets from Latin camera 'vaulted room'.
normal.cn: chamber 与 camera 是拉丁 camera「拱顶房间」的同源异形词。

normal.en: Real terms: rock-cut burial chamber, sealed burial chamber, royal burial chamber.
normal.cn: 真实术语：岩凿墓室、封闭墓室、王室墓室。

normal.en: The phrase names a function, not a material: brick, stone or bedrock all work.
normal.cn: 这个短语命名的是功能而非材料：砖、石或基岩都可以。

normal.en: Archaeology records the room as a unit with its own plan and contents.
normal.cn: 考古学把墓室当作带有独立平面与随葬品的单元来记录。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the phrase from a functional room in a tomb to its underground part, royal inner room, rock-cut form, archaeological unit, grave-goods room, family vault, and finally any sealed space.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着这个短语展开：先是墓中承担功能的房间，再到其地下部分、王陵内室、岩凿形式、考古单元、随葬品室、家族墓室，最后是任何被封存的空间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small stone room underground whose door is sealed by one slab.
core.cn: 核心意象：地下一间石砌小屋，门被一块石板封住。

branches.en: ROOM FOR THE BODY: the phrase names the space that receives the coffin, above or below the shaft.
branches.cn: 安放遗体的房间：这个短语指承接棺木的空间，无论在竖井之上还是之下。

branches.en: INNER ROOM: royal tombs and rock-cut tombs both need a named inner space.
branches.cn: 内室：王陵与岩凿墓都需要一个有名目的内部空间。

branches.en: RECORDED UNIT: excavation turns the room into a unit of plan and contents.
branches.cn: 被记录的单元：发掘把房间变成平面与随葬品的记录单元。

branches.en: GOODS AND FAMILY: side rooms hold offerings, and reopened rooms hold generations.
branches.cn: 随葬与家族：侧室放供品，反复开启的墓室安放数代人。

branches.en: SEALED SPACE: the metaphor keeps only the closed door and the undisturbed inside.
branches.cn: 封存空间：比喻只保留关闭的门与不被扰动的内部。

intro.en: The phrase is made of an Old English burial word and a Latin room word, so its affix list follows two families.
intro.cn: 这个短语由古英语的「埋葬」词与拉丁语的「房间」词构成，词缀表因此沿两条词族展开。

intro.en: Elite is Old French eslite, the chosen ones, from eslire, which goes back to Latin eligere, to pick out; the elite are simply those picked out of the rest.
intro.cn: elite 是古法语 eslite（被选中的人），来自 eslire，可上溯到拉丁语 eligere（挑出来）；精英就是从其余人里被挑出来的那批。

items.en: Latin legere means to gather or choose.
items.cn: 拉丁语 legere 意为收集或挑选。

items.en: Adding ex- gives eligere, to pick out.
items.cn: 加 ex- 构成 eligere，意为挑出来。

items.en: Old French eslite, from eslire, meant the chosen ones.
items.cn: 古法语 eslite 来自 eslire，意为被选中的人。

items.en: English took elite in the 18C for the best or the powerful few.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪借用 elite，指最优秀者或少数权贵。

items.en: Writers used elite for a social class set above the rest.
items.cn: 作家用 elite 指高于其余人的社会阶层。

items.en: Sport and education made elite a label for the top level.
items.cn: 体育与教育使 elite 成为最高水平的标签。

note.en: Elite and elect share the Latin root for choosing; elite names the chosen few, while elitism turns that into a doctrine about who should lead.
note.cn: elite 与 elect 共用拉丁语「挑选」的词根；elite 指被选中的少数人，elitism 则把它变成一套「谁该领导」的主张。

dict_mnemonic.text: elite 来自古法语 eslite「被选中的人」，词根是拉丁 eligere（e- 外 ＋ legere 挑）＝挑出来。所以 elite 的本义就是「被挑出来的那一批」：the elite 精英（集合名词，谓语可用复数），elite athletes 顶尖运动员，elite forces 精锐部队，the ruling elite 统治精英。加后缀派生：-ism → elitism 精英主义（认为该由少数优秀者领导），-ist → elitist 精英主义者（常带贬义）。同根词 elect 选举、select 挑选、eligible 符合条件的。近义 aristocracy 靠出身的贵族，vanguard 走在最前面的先锋，the cream of the crop 一批里最好的部分。注意 elite 作形容词时没有 -er/-est，比较级用 more elite。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外）＋ legere（挑选）→ eligere → 古法语 eslite（被选中者）→ elite（精英）

definition_zh: n. 售货亭，摊位；（电话、投票等的）隔间
definition_en: a small structure for selling or showing goods; also a small enclosed space such as a phone booth or a voting booth
core_image: 集市上一排蓝白条纹的小亭子
scene: 集市那天，每个摊位只用一块帆布与邻摊隔开。 At the fair, each booth was separated from the next by a single sheet of canvas.

definition_zh: 獾；纠缠不休；烦扰
definition_en: a burrowing mammal with a striped face; also, to pester someone persistently
core_image: 一只獾咬住裤脚不放，甩也甩不掉
scene: 弟弟一路追问个没完，直到姐姐松口。 He badgered his sister into lending the car.
sceneCN: 这里 badger 指「纠缠、烦扰」（第 2 个义项：不停追问）；句意：他软磨硬泡，姐姐终于把车借给了他。

derivatives.zh: 蜜獾（复合术语，以凶悍著称）

senses.title: The striped burrowing mammal
senses.definition: a heavy, short-legged mammal with a white-striped face that digs burrows
senses.definitionCN: 体壮腿短、面部有白色条纹、善掘洞的哺乳动物
senses.example: A badger crossed the lane at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时一只獾穿过小路。
senses.why: The animal itself is the word's root sense.
senses.whyCN: 动物本身即这个词的本义。

senses.title: To pester persistently
senses.definition: to harass or nag someone repeatedly until they give in
senses.definitionCN: 反复纠缠、唠叨，直至对方让步
senses.example: Reporters badgered the minister about the leak.
senses.exampleCN: 记者们就泄密事件纠缠部长不放。
senses.why: From the baiting sport: dogs pinned a badger in its hole and it fought back without yielding.
senses.whyCN: 源于逗獾游戏：犬在洞口围堵，獾拒不屈服，遂引申出「纠缠」。

senses.title: To urge relentlessly
senses.definition: to press someone with repeated demands or requests
senses.definitionCN: 以反复的要求或恳求催迫某人
senses.example: She badgered the office for a reply all week.
senses.exampleCN: 她整整一周催着办公室要答复。
senses.why: Persistence alone distinguishes it from mere asking.
senses.whyCN: 与普通请求之别只在「不停」。

senses.title: The baited animal in sport
senses.definition: in the old blood sport, the badger drawn from its sett to fight dogs
senses.definitionCN: 旧时血腥游戏里被从洞中诱出与犬相斗的獾
senses.example: Parliament banned badger baiting in 1835.
senses.exampleCN: 1835 年议会取缔了逗獾游戏。
senses.why: The verb was born inside this cruel custom.
senses.whyCN: 动词正是在这一残忍习俗中诞生的。

senses.title: Gruff, stubborn character
senses.definition: a person compared to the badger, ill-tempered or reclusive
senses.definitionCN: 被比作獾的人：脾气坏或喜独处
senses.example: The old badger of the village kept to his forge.
senses.exampleCN: 村里那位老倔头整天守着铁匠铺。
senses.why: The animal's surly look lent itself to the likeness.
senses.whyCN: 獾一脸倔相，自然被借来写人。

senses.title: Legal badgering of witnesses
senses.definition: harassing questioning of a witness, as objected in court
senses.definitionCN: 法庭上被异议的纠缠式盘问
senses.example: Counsel objected: the witness was being badgered.
senses.exampleCN: 律师提出异议：证人正受纠缠式盘问。
senses.why: Courtroom procedure froze the verb into a term of art.
senses.whyCN: 法庭程序把这个动词冻结成了术语。

senses.title: The badger game, a swindle
senses.definition: in slang, an extortion trick built on fabricated romance
senses.definitionCN: 俚语中，以虚构恋情为基础的敲诈骗局
senses.example: Victims of the badger game rarely went to the police.
senses.exampleCN: 仙人跳的受害者极少报警。
senses.why: The cornered-baiting image transferred to cornered victims.
senses.whyCN: 「被围堵的獾」意象转用于被围堵的受害者。

senses.title: Honey badger, emblem of grit
senses.definition: the honey badger as a popular emblem of fearless persistence
senses.definitionCN: 蜜獾作为流行文化中无畏坚韧的象征
senses.example: The startup's logo is a honey badger for a reason.
senses.exampleCN: 那家创业公司以蜜獾为标志是有原因的。
senses.why: The animal's refusal to retreat became internet legend.
senses.whyCN: 蜜獾从不后退，遂成网络传奇。

items.cn: 额部白斑使人联想其名出自 badge「徽章」。

items.en: An older theory ties badger to the itinerant dealer who carried goods by badger or bag.
items.cn: 旧说则把 badger 与背负行囊的流动商贩相联。

items.cn: 17、18 世纪动词义扩大为一切纠缠不休的烦扰。

items.en: The animal survives in countryside and mascot; the verb thrives in news and courtrooms.
items.cn: 动物义存于乡野与吉祥物，动词义活跃于新闻与法庭。

entries.definition: to beg persistently and urgently; formal register.
entries.definitionCN: 苦苦恳求；正式语域。

normalIntro.en: Picture a badger tugging your trouser cuff, refusing to let go.
normalIntro.cn: 想象一只獾咬着你的裤脚，说什么也不放。

normal.en: The verb grew from badger baiting: cornered, it never yields.
normal.cn: 动词源于逗獾游戏：被围堵的獾绝不屈服。

normal.en: badger someone into doing is the exam pattern.
normal.cn: badger someone into doing 是考试句型。

normal.en: Courtroom term: badgering the witness draws an objection.
normal.cn: 法庭术语：badgering the witness 会被法官制止。

normal.en: The white forehead stripe explains the badge theory.
normal.cn: 额部白条解释了 badge（徽章）学说。

normal.en: Pair it with hound and pester for the pestering family.
normal.cn: 与 hound、pester 成组记，同属纠缠词族。

abstract.en: Feel the small teeth that do not tire.
abstract.cn: 感受那副不知疲倦的小牙。

abstract.en: Badgering is patience weaponized.
abstract.cn: 纠缠是武装到牙齿的耐心。

abstract.en: Hear the same question for the ninth time.
abstract.cn: 听同一个问题被问到第九遍。

examples.en: The children badgered their father for a puppy all summer.
examples.cn: 孩子们磨了父亲一整个夏天，想要一只小狗。

examples.en: A family of badgers denned under the old barn.
examples.cn: 一窝獾在旧谷仓下安了家。

examples.en: Stop badgering me; I heard you the first time.
examples.cn: 别再烦我了，第一遍我就听见了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「八征」——他八次上门征询答案，磨得人不得安宁

root: 动物义 badger 约 16 世纪初见于英语，主流学说认为出自 badge「徽章」，指其额部白斑；旧说则联系「行商」一词。动词义 16 世纪生长于逗獾游戏（badger-baiting）：獾被犬围堵于洞口而拒不退让，遂引申为「纠缠不休」，后进入法律术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run on two tracks: the animal itself, and the human pestering the baiting sport bequeathed, from reporters to courtrooms to slang swindles.
sensesIntro.cn: 八义项沿两条线索：动物本身，以及逗獾游戏留下的人际纠缠——从记者追问到法庭盘问再到俚语骗局。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a striped face that will not let go, in the earth or at your elbow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张条纹脸不肯松口——无论在土里还是在你身边。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL SIDE: the mammal, the emblem, the stubborn neighbor.
branches.cn: 动物一面：獾本身、其象征、倔强的邻居。

branches.en: THE SPORT SIDE: the baiting pit where the verb was born.
branches.cn: 游戏一面：动词的诞生地——逗獾场。

branches.en: THE PESTERING SIDE: questions and requests without end.
branches.cn: 纠缠一面：没有穷尽的追问与请求。

branches.en: THE LEGAL SIDE: badgering the witness.
branches.cn: 法律一面：对证人的纠缠式盘问。

branches.en: THE SLANG SIDE: the swindle named for cornering.
branches.cn: 俚语一面：以围堵命名的骗局。

intro.en: Badger carries no living affix; its structure is a simple animal name turned verb.
intro.cn: badger 不含活跃词缀，其结构是单纯的动物名转动词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin enters here: the word is wholly English in formation, whatever its ultimate source.
latinIntro.cn: 与拉丁语无关：无论最终来源为何，构词全然是英语的。

items.example: an old sett in the wood

items.meaning: the sport of setting dogs on an animal

items.exampleCN: 被缠得不胜其烦的官员

definition_zh: 使改变方向；改寄；重定向；引导（精力、资金）
definition_en: to change the direction of something, to send it to a new place, or to turn resources toward a new purpose
core_image: 路口一块临时路牌，把整条车流斜斜地引向旁边那条街
scene: 施工队在路上竖了一块临时指示牌，把车流引到旁边的街道。 A temporary sign redirected the traffic into the next street.
sceneCN: 这里 redirect 指使改变方向（第 1 个义项：改变交通、水流等的走向）；句意为一块临时指示牌把车流引到旁边的街道。

pos.zh: 使改变方向；改寄；重定向；引导

senses.title: To redirect traffic
senses.definition: to change the course of vehicles, water or a moving flow
senses.definitionCN: 改变车辆、水流或任何流动之物的路线
senses.example: A temporary sign redirected the traffic into the next street.
senses.exampleCN: 一块临时指示牌把车流引到旁边的街道。
senses.why: The first sense is physical: a moving stream is turned to another channel.
senses.whyCN: 第一个义项是物理的：一股流动被引到另一条通道。

senses.title: To redirect a letter
senses.definition: to send a letter, call or address to a different destination
senses.definitionCN: 把信件、电话或地址送往另一个目的地
senses.example: The office redirected the letter to his new address.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室把那封信改寄到他的新地址。
senses.why: Here the flow is information, and it is sent elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 这里的流动是信息，被送往别处。

senses.title: To redirect funds
senses.definition: to turn money, effort or attention toward a new purpose
senses.definitionCN: 把金钱、精力或注意力转向新的用途
senses.example: The board redirected the budget toward repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会把预算转向修缮。
senses.why: The sense is strategic: the same resource, a new target.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是战略性的：同一份资源，换了一个目标。

intro.en: Redirect is re-, 'again', plus direct, from Latin dirigere, 'to set straight'.
intro.cn: redirect 是 re-（再次）加 direct，后者来自拉丁语 dirigere（使成直线、指向）。

items.en: Regere meant to rule or to guide straight.
items.cn: regere 意为统治或引直。

items.en: Dirigere meant to set something in a straight line.
items.cn: dirigere 意为把某物摆成直线。

items.en: English direct kept the sense of pointing.
items.cn: 英语的 direct 保留了「指向」的意思。

items.en: The prefix adds a second pointing elsewhere.
items.cn: 前缀加上第二次指向别处。

items.en: Offices and networks made the word common.
items.cn: 办公室与网络让这个词流行起来。

note.en: The look-alike group is the direct- family; the near-meaning group separates reroute, divert, channel and reassign.
note.cn: 形近组是 direct 词族；近义组把「改线」「改道」「引导」「重新分配」分开。

entries.definition: to point or manage.
entries.definitionCN: 指向；指挥。

entries.definition: the line along which something moves.
entries.definitionCN: 运动所沿的线。

entries.definition: an instruction about what to do.
entries.definitionCN: 关于怎么做的指示。

entries.definition: one who manages an organisation.
entries.definitionCN: 管理组织的人。

entries.definition: to send along a different route.
entries.definitionCN: 沿另一条路线发送。

entries.definition: to turn aside from a course.
entries.definitionCN: 使偏离原路线。

entries.definition: to guide through a particular path.
entries.definitionCN: 引导通过特定路径。

entries.definition: to give a new task or place.
entries.definitionCN: 重新分派任务或位置。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a temporary sign bending a whole stream of cars into a side street.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一块临时路牌把整条车流弯进侧街」的画面。

normal.en: Redirect is re plus direct: the pointing happens again, elsewhere.
normal.cn: redirect 是 re 加 direct：指向再做一次，指向别处。

normal.en: Picture the arrow on the sign turning forty degrees.
normal.cn: 想象牌子上的箭头转了四十度。

normal.en: Say ree-dih-REKT; the stress falls on REKT.
normal.cn: 读 ree-dih-REKT，重音在 REKT。

normal.en: Traffic, letters, money and attention can all be redirected.
normal.cn: 车流、信件、金钱和注意力都能被改向。

normal.en: Ask who raised the sign, and who pays for the detour.
normal.cn: 问是谁竖起了牌子，又是谁为绕路买单。

abstract.en: To redirect is to admit the original route was badly chosen.
abstract.cn: 改向就是承认原来的路线选错了。

abstract.en: Every detour is a small essay about priority.
abstract.cn: 每一次改道都是一篇关于优先级的小论文。

abstract.en: The word moves streams that have no opinion about their course.
abstract.cn: 这个词挪动的是对自己路线没有意见的流动。

examples.en: A temporary sign redirected the traffic into the next street.
examples.cn: 一块临时指示牌把车流引到旁边的街道。

examples.en: The office redirected the letter to his new address.
examples.cn: 办公室把那封信改寄到他的新地址。

examples.en: The board redirected the budget toward repairs.
examples.cn: 董事会把预算转向修缮。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（再）+ direct（指向）→ 把原来指向这边的，再指向别处。

root: 拉丁语 dirigere（使成直线、指向）→ re- + direct

sensesIntro.en: Three senses turn three flows: vehicles, information and resources.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项改的是三种流动：车辆、信息与资源。

core.en: A SIGN BENDING THE FLOW
core.cn: 把车流弯过去的牌子

branches.en: Vehicles or water sent along a new course.
branches.cn: 被引到新路线的车或水。

branches.en: A letter or call sent to another address.
branches.cn: 被送往另一地址的信或电话。

branches.en: Money or attention given a new target.
branches.cn: 被赋予新目标的钱或注意力。

branches.en: One turns a body, the other turns a message.
branches.cn: 一个转动实体，一个转动消息。

branches.en: Both decide where something should land.
branches.cn: 两者都在决定某物该落在哪里。

intro.en: The direct- family is about pointing: direct, direction, directive and director all stand on the Latin line of dirigere.
intro.cn: direct 词族讲的是「指向」：direct、direction、directive、director 都立在 dirigere 那条拉丁线上。

latinIntro.en: Latin dirigere, 'to set straight', gives direct; re- adds a second setting, this time toward a different point.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dirigere（摆直）给出 direct；re- 加上第二次摆放，这一次朝另一个点。
